column1: Single Cancel API for Bracket Orders
column41:
Currently, for Bracket Orders:

Before trigger: only one order and one gOrderId is generated, so a single cancel request works.
After trigger: three orders and three separate gOrderIds are generated, requiring three cancel requests.

Motilal Oswal requires a single cancel API that can cancel the complete bracket order irrespective of whether it is triggered or not.

(if SL cancelled by user automatically Trigger also gets cancel vice versa.)

column1: Enable single-request cancel for bracket order instead of multiple GorderId cancellations in REST API
column41:
In the current REST API implementation for bracket orders, three separate GorderIds are generated for a single bracket order. As a result, when the client needs to cancel the order, they are required to send multiple cancel requests for each individual GorderId.

The client wants cancellation of the entire bracket order in a single request instead of sending multiple cancel requests.

h3. *Current Behavior:*

* Three GorderIds are generated for one bracket order.
* Client must send multiple cancel requests (one per GorderId).

h3. *Expected Behavior:*

* Client should be able to cancel the complete bracket order using a single API request.
* System should internally handle cancellation of all associated GorderIds.

column1: Issue in ETF Strategy NAV Calculation Across Exchanges
column41:
Issue has been identified in the ETF Strategy NAV calculation.

Currently, the NAV is being calculated using NSE Current Assets values for both NSE and BSE records. However, NAV should be calculated separately for each exchange based on their respective Current Assets .

For the same ETF symbol, although the Units are same across exchanges, the Current Assets values differ. Despite this, the system is displaying the same NAV for both NSE and BSE.

*Example:*

||Date||Exchange||Current Assets (Rs)||Units||Expected NAV||
|26-08-2022|NSE|20760.12|240000|27.57|
|26-08-2022|BSE|1000.00|240000|Should be different|

*Expected Behavior:*
NAV should be calculated separately for each exchange using its respective Current Assets values.

*Actual Behavior:*
BSE NAV is displaying the same value as NSE NAV because the calculation is referencing NSE Current Assets instead of BSE-specific values.

Log Path :  [ftp://192.168.209.145/SUPPORT_TEAM_LIVE_ISSUES_2026/Kancjlochna_25-05-2026/|ftp://192.168.209.145/SUPPORT_TEAM_LIVE_ISSUES_2026/Kancjlochna_25-05-2026/]

{color:#ff5630}It is not an issue, client is using same scheme name for two different rule with different market capitalization and I am using scheme name as a unique key for ETF schemas {color}

{color:#ff5630}So I have given a solution to change scheme name which is not a temporary solution, {color}

{color:#ff5630}It is working as per implemented logic{color}

column1: Common logic for NNF and Algo ID
column41:
h3. Summary

Common classes need to be developed for NNF and Algo ID. These classes will handle all logic necessary for their creation based on various scenarios.

h3. Context

The development of these classes is essential for both Server and Client usage. They will ensure consistent functionality across different variations and scenarios.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* Develop common classes for NNF and Algo ID.
* Incorporate all logic required for their creation.
* Ensure usage on Server & Client is managed through functions within these classes.
* Achieve 100% test coverage for the classes.
* Write test cases using AI.
* Preferably, use AI for the entire class development process.

h3. Other information

Comprehensive Analysis: dNNFField and CAlgoID Components
Executive Summary
Based on the detailed analysis of the Fusion RHL trading system, I've identified the complete working mechanisms of dNNFField and CAlgoID (AlgoIDMapping) components, including admin update scenarios and immediate module propagation.

# Data Structures and Storage
dNNFField Components
Primary Structure: NNFNFiledStruct (ProcessArbitrageOrder/m_pNNFNFiledMap)
Exchange Details: Multiple ExchangeDetails for each exchange (NSEEQ, NSEFO, BSEEQ, BSEFO, etc.)
Database Table: NNFFieldTracker (PostgreSQL via CPostgresqlNNFFieldTracker)
Key Mapping: cGreekClientId ? NNFNFiledStruct (Abseil flat_hash_map)
CAlgoID (AlgoIDMapping) Components
Primary Structure: ALGOID_MAPPING (includes cAlgoID, cAlgoIdIBT, cAlgoIdDMA)
Database Table: AlgoIDMapping (PostgreSQL via CPostgresqlAlgoIDMapping)
Key Mapping: Composite key (lMemberId + iExchange + iExchangeSegment + iStrategyType)
Storage: Separate maps for vendor (g_pAlgoDetails) and in-house (g_pAlgoDetails_Inhouse)
# Admin Update Scenarios
dNNFField Admin Update Scenarios:
Initial Client Setup
Admin creates client in MasterAdmin
ClientCommunicator processes login request
sendLoginDetails() populates exchange-specific NNF fields
Entries inserted into NNFFieldTracker table
CNNFNFiledMap updated via ProcessArbitrageOrder
Client Login/Reauthentication
User authenticates
Multiple sendLoginDetails() calls for each enabled exchange
Exchange-specific NNF fields sent to Interactive modules
Interactive modules update local NNF structures
NNF Value Modification
Admin modifies NNF fields from MasterAdmin panel
Database update executed via ClientCommunicator
Maps reloaded or queried fresh from QuickInMemory for latest values
Changes become available via lookups on the next operation
PAN Number Updates
Admin updates client PAN
Propagation to NNF structures in map and database
Used for order validation and regulatory compliance
CAlgoID Admin Update Scenarios:
Initial System Setup
GSATS starts and calls SetupAlgoDetailsMap() (GSATS.cpp:12616)
Queries all records from AlgoIDMapping table via CInMemAlgoIDMapping
Builds in-memory maps (g_pAlgoDetails and g_pAlgoDetails_Inhouse)
New Algo ID Mapping Addition
Admin adds new algo mapping via MasterAdmin
ClientCommunicator processes IC_ALGOIDMAPPING_ADD_REQ request
AlgoIDMapping table updated via InsertData()
GSATS can reload mappings via SetupAlgoDetailsMap()
Algo ID Modification
Admin modifies existing algo ID
Update request processed by ClientCommunicator
Record updated in AlgoIDMapping table
Maps can be reloaded; new mapping becomes available on next lookup
Algo Category Changes
Update in database
Map reload triggered
New category used for strategy execution
# Immediate Update Propagation Flow
dNNFField Propagation to Modules:
Admin Update ? ClientCommunicator ? PostgreSQL NNFFieldTracker
        ?
      ProcessArbitrageOrder (m_pNNFNFiledMap reload/lookup)
        ?

GSATS/       NSEInteractive  ETIInteractive  BasketManagement
Basket       (Order     (Order Tracking) (PAN Lookup)
Management   Processing)
Immediate Update Points:

GSATS: Uses m_pNNFNFiledMap for PAN/Broker/Trader ID extraction (BasketManagement.cpp:2186, 7112, 8653)
NSEInteractive: Queries NNFFieldTracker for order details (FO_MARKET.cpp:3314-3320), uses hash tables (CRequestProcess.h:8499)
ETIInteractive: Maintains OrderInfoMap with getClOrdIdInNNFFieldTrackerTableAndMap() (BSEETIInteractive.cpp:24380-24395)
CAlgoID Propagation to Modules:

Immediate Update Points:

GSATS: SetAlgoIDandAlgoCategory() uses persisted maps; supports on-demand reload (ProcessArbitrageOrder.cpp:8244-8299)
Spread Strategies: SpreadIVOrder, RSMarketMaking call SetAlgoIDandAlgoCategory for each leg
NSEInteractive: Sets default algo ID if empty (CRequestProcess.h:5356, 5681, 7236)
Other Modules: GSJobbing, ScalpingGATS, GSStrategyCommunicator, GSOM, ETF strategies
4. All Related Components
Core Components:
Database Layer
CPostgresqlNNFFieldTracker (QuickInMemory/PostgresqlNNFFieldtracker.cpp)
CPostgresqlAlgoIDMapping (QuickInMemory/PostgresqlAlgoIDMapping.cpp)
Tables: NNFFieldTracker and AlgoIDMapping (PostgreSQL)
Memory Management
CNNFNFiledMap (ProcessArbitrageOrder/m_pNNFNFiledMap)
g_pAlgoDetails and g_pAlgoDetails_Inhouse (GSATS)
Communication
ClientCommunicator (DBOperations.cpp:ProcessAlgoIDAddRequest, ResponseProcessing.cpp:sendLoginDetails)
MasterAdmin (Admin interface)
Consumer Modules
GSATS: ProcessArbitrageOrder, BasketManagement, SpreadIVOrder, RSMarketMaking
NSEInteractive: EQ_MARKET, FO_MARKET, CURR_MARKET, CRequestProcess
ETIInteractive: BSEETIInteractive, MCXETIInteractive
Other Strategies: GreekExecutionAlgos, FourLegSpreadIV, SixLegStrategy, ETF strategies
Integration Points
Order Placement: AlgoID resolution via maps + NNF details from QuickInMemory
Basket Management: PAN number extraction from CNNFNFiledMap
Spread Orders: Consistent algo ID assignment across legs; NNF context per leg
Tracking: Interactive modules query NNFFieldTracker via QuickInMemory
5. Real-time and On-demand Reload Mechanisms
dNNFField Reload:
Login/login-resync flows trigger sendLoginDetails() which updates module state and pushes latest NNF values
Interactive modules periodically query NNFFieldTracker via QuickInMemory for order tracking and reconciliation
Maps are updated at startup and maintained throughout runtime (insert_or_assign)
CAlgoID Reload:
SetupAlgoDetailsMap() performs full reload from AlgoIDMapping table on demand
Triggered on GSATS initialization or via admin-driven reload signals
Maps remain in memory while active; new mappings are available on next lookup after reload
Key Characteristics:
Dual-layer Architecture: Persistent database + in-memory cache for fast access
Lookup-based Consistency: Maps serve authoritative lookups; QuickInMemory surfaces fresh data to interactive modules
Performance Optimized: O(1) lookup latency via hash maps; bulk operations are database-driven (InsertData/UpdateData via Postgresql* classes)
Multi-exchange Support: Exchange-specific NNF fields per client (NSEEQ, NSEFO, BSEEQ, BSEFO, etc.) with vendor/in-house separation for algo mappings

# A feature is required to identify and recognize orders that were not sent to the exchange, i.e., orders for which the 5511 order confirmation Greekcode has not been received.
# Note: Orders may get stuck in cases where the request is sent to Interactive but no response is received due to Interactive crash, exchange logoff in between, or Interactive getting stuck.  



Solution:

Provide a “cancel-stuck-orders” command line switch in CC which will cancel all the orders which match the criteria. To avoid accidental usage, a passphrase will be asked and process will begin only if the correct passphrase is entered.

column1: FIX Session Disconnection Issue – BOD Schedule Change Impact (Server 2011) - Nomura
column41:
*Issue Summary:*

Following the BOD schedule adjustment from 7:00 AM to 4:20 AM (to accommodate the FO desk's 5:00 AM IST / 11:30 PM GMT FIX session connection requirement), we are experiencing persistent FIX session disconnections and message rejection errors.

 

*Root Cause:*

The FIX session is being initiated before the GMT date rollover (23:30 GMT on the previous calendar day). This causes the FIX Library to treat the session as belonging to the previous day and prevents proper sequence number reset. Consequently:

* Initial connection attempts are rejected with error code *"58=MsgSeqNum too low"*
* Sequence numbers are not reset upon connection establishment
* All incoming requests during this period are rejected due to sequence mismatch

 

*Current Behaviour:*

# *23:30:00 GMT (19 May):* First login request received
# *23:30:00 – 23:34:04 GMT:* Three login attempts rejected (sequence mismatch)
# *23:34:04 GMT:* Connection established successfully
# *23:59:59 GMT:* Session auto-disconnects at day boundary
# *00:00:04 GMT (20 May):* New login requests rejected – sequence numbers already consumed from previous day's session.

 

*Temporary Workaround:*

Manually deleting the sequence file from the FIXENGINE_FileStore folder and restarting the FIX engine allows reconnection, but the issue recurs at the GMT midnight boundary.

 

*Recommended Actions:*

# Adjust the BOD schedule to occur after the GMT date rollover (post-00:00 GMT) to ensure FIX sessions initiate on the correct calendar day
# Verify FIX Library configuration for proper session date handling across day boundaries
# Review sequence number reset logic in the FIX engine initialization
# Implement automated sequence file cleanup as part of the BOD process if manual intervention is currently required.

 

Please advise on the feasibility of adjusting the BOD schedule or implementing a permanent fix to the FIX session management logic.

TCP Blackhole Detection and Recovery Improvements
column41:
h3. Description

Current TCP connection handling may take too long to detect blackholed or silently broken network paths, especially in low-latency/trading environments.

This task evaluates and implements improved TCP liveness detection mechanisms to reduce failover/reconnect latency and improve connection resiliency.

The discussion covers three levels of detection:

# Kernel TCP keepalive
# {{TCP_USER_TIMEOUT}}
# Application-level heartbeats

h2. Problem Statement

In certain network failure scenarios:

* packets are silently dropped
* connection appears established
* TCP retransmission may continue for several minutes

This creates:

* delayed failover
* stale exchange sessions
* blocked order flow
* increased recovery time

Need faster and deterministic dead connection detection.



h1. Option 1 — TCP Keepalive

Enable TCP keepalive and tune kernel probe timings.

h3. Socket Configuration

{noformat}int yes = 1;
setsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_KEEPALIVE, &yes, sizeof(yes));

int idle = 10;
setsockopt(fd, IPPROTO_TCP, TCP_KEEPIDLE, &idle, sizeof(idle));

int intvl = 2;
setsockopt(fd, IPPROTO_TCP, TCP_KEEPINTVL, &intvl, sizeof(intvl));

int cnt = 3;
setsockopt(fd, IPPROTO_TCP, TCP_KEEPCNT, &cnt, sizeof(cnt));{noformat}

h3. Behavior

*  After 10 seconds of idle: 
**  kernel sends keepalive probes 
*  Probe interval: 
**  every 2 seconds 
*  After 3 missed probes: 
**  socket disconnected 
*  Approximate failure detection: 
**  ~16 seconds 

h3. Pros

*  Easy to implement 
*  Kernel-managed 
*  Low overhead 
*  Improves dead-peer detection 

h3. Limitations

*  Effective mainly for idle connections 
*  Less useful while application traffic is actively flowing 
*  Detects TCP stack reachability only 
*  Does not verify application responsiveness 

----

h1. Option 2 — TCP_USER_TIMEOUT 

Configure maximum time for unacknowledged TCP data.

h3. Socket Configuration

{noformat}int timeout_ms = 15000;

setsockopt(
    fd,
    IPPROTO_TCP,
    TCP_USER_TIMEOUT,
    &timeout_ms,
    sizeof(timeout_ms));{noformat}

h3. Behavior

If transmitted data is not ACKed within:

*  15 seconds 

Kernel aborts the socket.

h3. Why This Helps

Directly addresses:

*  blackholed network paths 
*  stalled ACKs 
*  silent packet drops 

Provides significantly faster failure detection than default TCP retransmission behavior.

h3. Advantages

*  Works during active traffic 
*  Better suited for low-latency/trading systems 
*  Faster recovery from broken paths 
*  Predictable fail-fast behavior 

----

h1. Option 3 — Application Heartbeats 

h3. Exchange connectivity issue detected.
No heartbeat received for 3 consecutive intervals.
Connection marked unhealthy. Starting disconnect and recovery process.

----

h1. Expected Outcome of option 1,2 & 3

*  Faster dead connection detection 
*  Reduced reconnect latency 
*  Improved resiliency against blackholed paths 
*  More deterministic exchange connectivity behavior 
*  Better failover characteristics for low-latency systems

h3. 

----

h1. *Option 4 — Configure Socket Timeouts and TCP Buffer Sizes for Improved Responsiveness and Throughput*

h3. Description

This task introduces socket-level timeout handling and TCP buffer tuning to improve connection responsiveness, prevent indefinite blocking, and optimize throughput for high-volume/low-latency communication.

The implementation configures:

* Receive timeout ({{SO_RCVTIMEO}})
* Send timeout ({{SO_SNDTIMEO}})
* TCP send buffer size ({{SO_SNDBUF}})
* TCP receive buffer size ({{SO_RCVBUF}})

These settings improve runtime stability and handling of slow, stalled, or burst-heavy network conditions.

----

h1. Timeout Configuration

h3. Code

{noformat}struct timeval timeout;
timeout.tv_sec = 3;
timeout.tv_usec = 0;
{noformat}

h3. Meaning

Defines a socket timeout value of:

{noformat}3 seconds
{noformat}

Where:

||Field||Meaning||
|{{tv_sec}}|Seconds|
|{{tv_usec}}|Microseconds|

So:

{noformat}tv_sec  = 3
tv_usec = 0
{noformat}

means:

{noformat}3.0 seconds
{noformat}

This timeout value is later applied to socket send and receive operations.

----

h1. Receive Timeout ({{SO_RCVTIMEO}})

h3. Code

{noformat}if (setsockopt(m_iServer_fd,
               SOL_SOCKET,
               SO_RCVTIMEO,
               &timeout,
               sizeof(timeout)) < 0)
{
    std::cout<<"Warning: set sock option Failed to set SO_RCVTIMEO "<<m_iPortNumber;
}
{noformat}

----

h2. Purpose

Configures maximum blocking duration for socket receive operations.

Applies to:

* {{recv()}}
* {{read()}}
* socket receive-related operations

----

h2. Behavior

If no data is received within:

{noformat}3 seconds
{noformat}

the receive operation times out and returns an error.

Typical error:

* {{EAGAIN}}
* {{EWOULDBLOCK}}

(depending on operating system behavior)

----

h2. Benefits

Prevents:

* indefinite blocking
* hung receive operations
* stalled network reads

Improves:

* responsiveness
* failure detection
* reconnect handling

----

h1. Send Timeout ({{SO_SNDTIMEO}})

h3. Code

{noformat}if (setsockopt(m_iServer_fd,
               SOL_SOCKET,
               SO_SNDTIMEO,
               &timeout,
               sizeof(timeout)) < 0)
{
    std::cout<<"Warning: set sock option Failed to set SO_SNDTIMEO"<<m_iPortNumber;
}
{noformat}

----

h2. Purpose

Configures maximum blocking duration for socket send operations.

Applies to:

* {{send()}}
* {{write()}}

----

h2. Behavior

If outgoing data cannot be queued/transmitted within:

{noformat}3 seconds
{noformat}

the send operation fails with timeout-related error.

This can occur when:

* peer stops reading
* network congestion exists
* kernel send buffer becomes full

----

h2. Benefits

Prevents:

* indefinitely blocked send operations
* application thread hangs
* delayed recovery from stalled connections

----

h1. TCP Send Buffer ({{SO_SNDBUF}})

h3. Code

{noformat}int sndbuf = 262144; // 256KB

if (setsockopt(m_iServer_fd,
               SOL_SOCKET,
               SO_SNDBUF,
               &sndbuf,
               sizeof(sndbuf)) < 0)
{
    std::cout<<"Warning: set sock option Failed to set SO_SNDBUF"<<m_iPortNumber;
}
{noformat}

----

h2. Purpose

Increases kernel TCP send buffer size to:

{noformat}256 KB
{noformat}

----

h2. Behavior

Allows kernel to queue larger amounts of outgoing TCP data before blocking application sends.

Improves:

* throughput
* burst traffic handling
* network efficiency

----

h2. Benefits

Useful for:

* high-throughput systems
* market data streaming
* low-latency communication
* burst-heavy traffic patterns

Reduces:

* frequent send blocking
* packet pacing issues

----

h1. TCP Receive Buffer ({{SO_RCVBUF}})

h3. Code

{noformat}int rcvbuf = 262144; // 256KB

if (setsockopt(m_iServer_fd,
               SOL_SOCKET,
               SO_RCVBUF,
               &rcvbuf,
               sizeof(rcvbuf)) < 0)
{
    std::cout<<"Warning: set sock option Failed to set SO_RCVBUF"<<m_iPortNumber;
}
{noformat}

----

h2. Purpose

Increases kernel TCP receive buffer size to:

{noformat}256 KB
{noformat}

----

h2. Behavior

Allows kernel to temporarily buffer larger amounts of incoming TCP data before application consumption.

Improves:

* burst absorption
* packet handling stability
* receive-side throughput

----

h2. Benefits

Helps prevent:

* receive buffer overflow
* packet drops
* TCP backpressure during traffic bursts

Especially important for:

* market data feeds
* exchange connectivity
* high-frequency message bursts

----

h1. Expected Outcome

After applying these socket configurations:

* socket operations fail faster under stalled conditions
* application avoids indefinite blocking
* network responsiveness improves
* throughput handling improves
* burst traffic handling becomes more stable
* connection recovery becomes faster and more deterministic

----

h1. Notes

* These are socket-level configurations applied per connection.
* Actual kernel buffer allocation may differ depending on OS/network stack behavior.
* Linux may internally increase configured buffer values beyond requested size.
* Timeout behavior may vary slightly across platforms.
* Option 4 has already been implemented in the {{console_rhl8(1209)}} branch, but it is not present in the {{develope_3009}} branch. Therefore, we will implement this change only for the {{3009}} branch.

column1: NSE EQ and FO Exchange Login Failure Due to Connection Reset During SSL Communication
column41:
NSE EQ and FO exchange login was not working even though interactive telnet connectivity to the exchange server IP and port was successful. Initially, connectivity was verified through telnet for both NSE EQ and FO exchanges, and the connection was established properly. 

After that, exchange login was tested using both the new encryption mechanism and without the new encryption mechanism, but in both cases the login process failed. As per the logs, the SSL connection was established successfully, the NSE Gateway CA certificate was verified successfully, and socket write operations were also completed successfully. 

However, during the socket read process, the application received {{SSL_Error=5}} with {{errno: 104 (Connection reset by peer)}}, after which the secure socket connection was closed and the process thread exited. 

Due to this issue, users were unable to log in to NSE EQ and FO exchanges.

column1: DAILY Position RESTAPI Returning Other Dealer Data in getStrategyNameWiseNetPositionDetail Response
column41:
While using the {{getStrategyNameWiseNetPositionDetail}} endpoint with {{DEALER_2}}, order responses belonging to another dealer ({{DEALER_1}}) are also being returned in the response, which should not occur.

Details from the ADMIN side:

* {{RETAILER_1}} is mapped with both dealers: {{DEALER_1}} and {{DEALER_2}}.
* In the REST API license mapping, only {{DEALER_2}} is mapped.
* {{DEALER_1}} is not mapped in the REST API license.

The endpoint response should return only {{DEALER_2}} related order data.

A similar functionality is required as currently implemented in CTCL:

* If a {{RETAILER}} is mapped in Dealer Client Mapper and the *View Orders* option is *ticked*, then the dealer should be able to view positions/orders of other dealers for that specific retailer.
* If the *View Orders* option is *unticked* in Dealer Client Mapper, then no dealer should be able to view positions/orders of other dealers for the same retailer.

Currently, this endpoint works correctly when fetching {{EXPIRY}} positions. The issue occurs only while fetching {{DAILY}} positions.

Endpoint:
{{http://192.168.207.18:3434/getStrategyNameWiseNetPositionDetail?gscid=RUSHI45}}

column1: Enhancement in GEA TWAP Algo – Slice Count Configuration for OFF-LIMIT Orders
column41:
+*Proposed Enhancement:*+ 

A new setting shall be introduced in GEA to allow configuration of the “No. of Slices” specifically for TWAP Algo orders executed under OFF-LIMIT conditions.

The configured slice count shall be considered by the TWAP engine during order slicing and execution.

----

+*The following validations shall be applicable:*+

* Field shall accept numeric values only.
* Minimum allowed value: 1
* Maximum allowed value: Configurable/System-defined limit.
* Blank value handling:
** If blank, existing default slicing logic shall continue.
* Negative or zero values shall not be accepted.

----

+*When a TWAP Algo order is placed with OFF-LIMIT enabled:*+

* System shall read the configured OFF-LIMIT Slice Count.
* Slice quantity calculation shall follow existing TWAP quantity distribution logic.
* Remaining quantity (if any due to rounding) shall be adjusted in the final slice.

----

+*This enhancement shall be applicable for:*+

* TWAP Algo Orders
* OFF-LIMIT enabled execution flow
* All supported order entry sources:
** FIX to IOB to GEA
** IOB to GEA
** Direct GEA orders

----

+*System shall reject order processing with appropriate error message in below cases:*+

||Scenario||Message||
|Invalid slice count|Invalid OFF-LIMIT Slice Count|
|Slice count exceeds allowed limit|Slice Count exceeds maximum permissible limit|

Exchange Placed Order via GEA shall not cancel if quantity modification received upside or quantity modification received for downside but more than traded quantity.

Conditions

Allowed modifications: 

# *Upsize* =Total quantity 1000, Traded quantity 300, exchange pending quantity 700 → Modification received from 1000>2000 quantity = after accepting this modification 700 pending quantity will be stay in exchange as it is and algo will bid for additional 1000 quantity.
# *Downsize* = Total quantity 1000, Traded quantity 700, exchange pending quantity 100 → Modification received from 1000>800 quantity = after accepting this modification, 100 pending quantity from exchange  will be stay in exchange as it is and algo will modify to 800 total quantity.
# *Downsize less than exchange pending quantity* = Total quantity 1000, Traded quantity 700, exchange pending quantity 100 → Modification received from 1000>700 quantity = *Do not allow to modify.*

column1: Enable Upward Quantity Modification for Completed FIX Orders on Same Parent Line
column41:
Enable Upward Quantity Modification for Completed FIX Orders on Same Parent Line



*Summary:*
Currently, the system restricts quantity modification once an order is fully executed. This feature aims to allow *upward quantity modification on the same FIX parent order line*, even if the order is completed, without requiring a new order placement.

*Business Need:*
Institutional and algorithmic trading workflows require flexibility to increase order quantities without creating new FIX orders. Allowing modification on the same order improves:

* Order traceability
* Reduced operational overhead
* Better alignment with client trading strategies

*Current Behavior:*

* System rejects modification if order is fully executed
* Error: _Modification not allowed / quantity constraints_
* Users must place a new order

*Proposed Behavior:*

* Allow *increase in total order quantity* even if:
** Order is fully executed
** Order is partially executed
* System should:
** Treat modification as *reopening/extending the same parent order*
** Maintain audit trail of modifications

column1: VEDL Order Execution Issue During Demerger - Manual Intervention Required and Resolved - Nomura
column41:
Facing order execution issue that occurred today with the VEDL script due to its demerger and subsequent re-listing.

 

*Issue Overview:*

* *Script:* VEDL
* *Event:* Demerger and re-listing
* *Problem:* FIX orders getting rejected due to incorrect segment routing
* *Status:* Issue resolved through manual intervention

 

*Detailed Timeline:*

*9:00 AM - 9:45 AM (Pre-Open Session):*

* All FIX orders for VEDL script were being rejected
* Root Cause Identified: Orders were being sent with RL order type instead of CB order type
* Action Taken: Manually changed order type from RL to CB
* Result: Existing orders could be executed, but no new orders were received during this period

*9:45 AM - 10:00 AM (Extended Pre-Open Monitoring):*

* Maintained CB order type configuration to observe system behaviour
* Objective: To check if the system would automatically switch from CB to RL order type after pre-open closure
* Decision: Kept manual changes active until 10:00 AM for monitoring

*10:00 AM onwards (Normal Market Hours):*

* New Issue: Orders started getting rejected again
* Cause: System was now sending new orders to exchange with CB order type instead of required RL order type
* Final Resolution: Manually changed order type from CB to RL through DPR window
* Outcome: All orders began working properly after switching to RL order type

*Key Learnings:*

# During demerger re-listing events, orders should use RL order type
# CB order type works during pre-open but causes rejections in normal trading hours
# Proper configuration for re-listed scripts requires RL order type throughout the trading session

 

*Current Status:*  All VEDL orders are now processing normally with RL segment configuration.

column41:
After Import DPR file its updated in DB and shared memory also sent to clients & respective application like RMS,GATS, JOBBING etc. in case of Bcast 1 or GMBS respective application send subscript’s token  DPR information to connected clients. In case of Bcast 2, clients receive data directly from the exchange via UDP, so the server has no token subscription details and cannot send DPR updates in optimus Branch . for sending DPR information for Bcast 2 clients, a separate class is created in the communicator instead of the broadcast component to avoid increased IPC load and if we change in broadcast then we have to do changes for all broadcast applications. In This class we maintain Bcast 2 client Details with Subscription token details. Only updated DPR information should be sent to Client or other application. Same DPR features of Bcast 2 we can use for first time token subscription data like Depth, TER, DPR , etc.





----

h1. *DPR Update and Distribution Mechanism*

h2. *1. Overview*

This document describes the mechanism for processing and distributing DPR (Daily Price Range) data after it is imported into the system. It covers behavior across different broadcast modes (Bcast 1 and Bcast 2), associated applications, and the design decisions taken to optimize performance and scalability.

----

h2. *2. DPR Import Flow*

# *DPR File Import*
#* Upon importing the DPR file, the data is:
#** Persisted in the *database (DB)*.
#** Updated in *shared memory* for fast access.
# *Data Propagation*
#* Once updated, DPR data is:
#** Sent to connected clients.
#** Distributed to internal applications such as:
#*** RMS
#*** GATS
#*** JOBBING
#*** Other dependent systems

----

h2. *3. Broadcast Modes Handling*

h3. *3.1 Bcast 1 (Subscription-Based Distribution)*

* In Bcast 1 mode:
** Respective applications maintain *subscription details (token-based)*.
** Applications send subscribed token information to the server.
** DPR updates are filtered based on these subscriptions.
** Only relevant DPR data is forwarded to:
*** Connected clients
*** Internal applications

h4. *Key Characteristics*

* Token subscription available at server level
* Selective data distribution
* Lower unnecessary data transmission

----

h3. *3.2 Bcast 2 (Exchange-Driven Distribution via UDP)*

* In Bcast 2 mode:
** Clients receive market data *directly from the exchange via UDP*.
** The server:
*** Does *not maintain token subscription details*
*** Cannot rely on application-level subscription tracking

h4. *Problem*

* DPR updates cannot be distributed using the existing broadcast mechanism (e.g., Optimus Branch), because:
** No subscription context is available at the server level

----

h2. *4. Solution Design for Bcast 2*

h3. *4.1 Dedicated Communicator Class*

To handle DPR distribution for Bcast 2:

* A *separate class* is implemented within the *communicator module*.
* This avoids modifying the existing broadcast component.

h4. *Reasons for Separate Implementation*

* Prevents *increased IPC (Inter-Process Communication) load*
* Avoids *system-wide changes* affecting all broadcast applications
* Maintains *modularity and backward compatibility*

----

h3. *4.2 Subscription Management in Communicator*

* The communicator class:
** Maintains *client details*
** Tracks *token subscription information* for Bcast 2 clients

h4. *Responsibilities*

* Register client subscriptions
* Maintain token-wise mapping
* Enable targeted DPR distribution

----

h2. *5. DPR Update Distribution Logic*

* Only *updated DPR entries* are sent:
** Avoids redundant data transmission
** Improves performance and network efficiency

h3. *Flow*

# Detect DPR updates
# Identify subscribed tokens (from communicator for Bcast 2)
# Send only changed DPR data to:
#* Clients
#* Relevant applications

----

h2. *6. Reusability for Other Market Data*

The Bcast 2 communicator-based approach can also be reused for:

* First-time token subscription data
* Other market data types such as:
** Depth
** TER
** DPR
** Similar real-time feeds

----

h2. *7. Benefits of the Approach*

* *Optimized Performance*
** Reduced IPC overhead
** Efficient data filtering
* *Scalability*
** Supports growing number of Bcast 2 clients
* *Modularity*
** No changes required in existing broadcast framework
* *Reusability*
** Applicable for multiple data types beyond DPR

----

h2. *8. Summary*

* DPR data is updated in DB and shared memory after import.
* Bcast 1 uses application-driven token subscriptions.
* Bcast 2 lacks server-side subscription awareness due to direct UDP feed.
* A dedicated communicator class is introduced for Bcast 2:
** Maintains subscriptions
** Sends only updated DPR data
* The same mechanism can be extended to other market data feeds.

column1: Motilal Oswal – Requirement to merge GetSessionId and greekLogin APIs
column41:
As part of a new requirement from Motilal Oswal Financial Services, we need to merge the existing GetSessionId and greekLogin APIs into a single endpoint.

During analysis, the following challenges were identified:

Latency Impact
The merged API will internally call two services, which may increase response time and introduce timeout handling complexities.
Error Handling

column1: Validation Restriction for Dividend Entry in Bank Import Payment/Receipt Voucher CSV Upload
column41:
Currently, in *Bank Import → Payment/Receipt CSV Upload*, users are able to record *dividend receipts* under the *Receipt Voucher* type.

This approach is incorrect because when dividends are entered through the Receipt Voucher, the system does not capture or track *which specific stock the dividend was received from*. This results in loss of important reference information and affects accurate tracking and reporting of dividend income.

*Requirement:*
A validation check needs to be implemented to prevent this scenario.

*Proposed Validation Logic:*

* If a user selects or inputs a *Dividend Account* while creating a *Receipt Voucher*, the system should *not allow the entry to be saved or processed*.
* The system should display an appropriate validation message informing the user that dividend entries cannot be recorded using the Receipt Voucher.

*Suggested Validation Message:*
“Dividend receipts cannot be recorded through the Receipt Voucher. Please record dividend income using the dividend voucher.”

column1: Bracket Order API allows invalid inputs without enforcing required validations.
column41:
Expected Validations

For BUY Orders

⦁	Trigger Price ≤ Price
⦁	Trigger Price ≥ Stop Loss (SL) Price
⦁	Target Price ≥ Price
⦁	Stop Loss Price ≤ Price and ≤ Target Price

For SELL Orders

⦁	Trigger Price ≥ Price
⦁	Trigger Price ≤ Stop Loss (SL) Price
⦁	Target Price ≤ Price
⦁	Stop Loss Price ≥ Price and ≥ Target Price

General Validations (Both Buy & Sell)

⦁	Bracket Order allowed only with Day validity
⦁	Bracket Order allowed only for Intraday
⦁	Bracket Order should not be accepted with zero price

*Note: Above validations should be for New order and modify order.*



*Expected Behavior for Bracket Orders (BO) Modification:*

*1.Validity Modification (Day → ?)*

Expected: NOT ALLOWED

Bracket Orders are strictly Intraday products
Validity is always Day
You should NOT be able to modify validity

Rule:
Validity = DAY → Fixed
Any attempt to modify →  Reject

*2.Order Type Modification*

Expected: NOT ALLOWED

Once placed as Bracket Order, it must remain BO
Cannot convert:

BO → Regular
BO → Cover Order 

Rule:
order_type = BO → Immutable

*3.After Bracket Order Execution (Leg Behavior)*

When main order executes, two legs are created:

Target Order
Stop Loss Order

*4.Modification Rules for Target & Stop Loss*

* Price Modification

Expected: ALLOWED

* Quantity Modification

Expected: NOT ALLOWED

+*Dealers comments:*+

Today we had received an order from BAJAJ AMC for BFFLX to buy 33975 qty of MFSL. Initial order was received at 11:15 AM with a price limit of INR 1675/- per share.

 

By 15:18, total pending qty was 13841 and we got a price revision from counterparty (1690).

 

Usual steps in such cases are:

 

# Accept price modification on Fixed book, which we did. This is usually just a click to `Accept` modification in the order.
# Upon accepting, greeksoft asks us whether we wish to convert price in the Algo from earlier rate to revised rate. We accepted the same.
# Now since this revision was given 10 mins prior to close, the algo also had to run until only 15:20. Hence I stopped algo and checked remaining qty on IOB window
# Pending qty to place and trade was 13841, I then bought 13841 qty through the IOB window upto price limit and the order got executed
# The IOB window never over executes any fixed line orders and hence if we were placing any quantity more than order received to us by the AMC, the order should be rejected.

 

Below is an illustration of IOB window, in the screenshot you see Rem. Place and Rem. Trade columns, in case remaining qty for any trade is 100 and we try to place 101 qty, the order gets rejected, hence there should never have been additional execution:

column1: IBT Mobile App: Apollo Micro Systems Sell Order Rejected as “Unauthorized DP holding sell” Despite Successful EDIS Status
column41:
In CTCL Terminal, the EDIS Report tab showed a successful EDIS authorization status for all stocks, including *Apollo Micro Systems Ltd*, across multiple attempts.

The user had completed the *EDIS process from CDSL* through the IBT Mobile App, and the same successful status was reflected in CTCL Terminal.

However, when the user tried to place a sell order for Apollo Micro Systems Ltd shares, the system rejected the order with the error message: *“Unauthorized DP holding sell not allowed for User”.*

The user was able to sell other shares that were EDIS-authorized without any issues.

For Apollo Micro Systems Ltd specifically, although the system displayed a successful EDIS status on all three attempts, the user had to complete the EDIS process three times via IBT Mobile App before the sell order was finally accepted and executed successfully.

Two-Factor Authentication API
column41:
As part of the API being used as platform to develop a web/mobile UI, we need to develop API endpoints to support two-factor authentication and related endpoints.



Use cases:

*Forgot / Reset Password*

* App will call the ForgotPassword API endpoint which will accept
** If details match, an OTP will be sent to the users mobile phone
* App will call the ValidateOTP API endpoint with the gscid and OTP
** If details match, a ResetPassword Special JWT token will be returned
* App will call the ResetPassword API endpoint with the gscid, Special JWT, password, confirm_password
* Password will be reset
* Reset password flow is complete

*Regular Login Flow*

* App will call the GenerateOTP API endpoint with the gscid and password
** If the credentails match, an OTP will be sent to the users mobile phone
* App will call the JLoginNew_JWT API endpoint with the gscid, password, OTP and other details
** If the credentails match, Regular JWT token will be returned
** This token can be used for the trading api including websocket

column1: Today's P&L and Total P&L required for Future and option carryforward record in mobile app Like Equity Holdings
column41:
Today's P&L required for Future and option carryforward record in mobile app Like Equity holdings.

Currently for equity holdings we have provision where user we get both P&L Today’s and Total.

Today’s P&L calculation :  Market Price - Close price 

Total P&L calculation : Market Price - Average(Holding Price) price 

The same P&L calculations should be implemented for *Options and Futures carryforward positions*.

h3. *Options Example:*

If a user buys a call option of Reliance at ₹5, with:

* Current Price = ₹9
* Previous Close Price = ₹7
* Quantity = 500

Then the system should display:

* *Today’s P&L* = (9 – 7) × 500 = ₹1,000
* *Total P&L* = (9 – 5) × 500 = ₹2,000

----

h3. *Futures Example:*

If a user buys a Reliance futures contract at ₹1300, with:

* Current Price = ₹1380
* Previous Close Price = ₹1350
* Quantity = 500

Then the system should display:

* *Today’s P&L* = (1380 – 1350) × 500 = ₹15,000
* *Total P&L* = (1380 – 1300) × 500 = ₹40,000

column41:
h3. *Description:*

Develop a centralized module in utilities section where users can add and track financial obligations such as SIPs, Insurance, Loan EMIs, Post Office schemes, Credit Card bills, and Subscriptions. The system should generate due dates based on defined frequency and send timely reminders.

----

h3. *Scope:*

* User can manually create, edit, and delete plans
* System generates recurring due dates
* Reminder notifications for upcoming and overdue payments
* Dashboard to view upcoming dues and active commitments

----

h3. *Supported Plan Types:*

* SIP
* Insurance (LIC / Mediclaim)
* Loan EMI
* Post Office योजनाएँ
* Credit Card Bills
* Subscriptions (OTT / SaaS)
* Others

----

h3. *Key Fields:*

* Plan Type
* Provider Name
* Amount
* Frequency (Monthly / Quarterly / Yearly / One-time)
* Due Date / Due Day
* Start Date / End Date
* Reminder Preferences (T-1, T-3, T-7)
* Trial End Date (Subscriptions)
* Notes / Reference ID

----

h3. *Functional Requirements:*

# System shall allow users to create plans with recurrence.
# System shall generate upcoming due instances (at least next 3 months).
# System shall send reminders via Email/WhatsApp/In-app:
#* Before due date (configurable)
#* On due date
# System shall provide dashboard widgets:
#* Upcoming Dues

----

h3. *Special Logic:*

* Credit card dues may vary → allow manual override of due date
* Subscription alerts to include renewal reminders and free trial expiry
* Auto-debit flag to differentiate informational vs actionable reminders

----

h3. *Non-Functional Requirements:*

* Daily scheduler (cron) for reminder processing
* Scalable for multiple plans per user
* High reliability for notification delivery

combined derivatives and segment-wise margin capping control
column41:
combined derivatives and segment-wise margin capping control

System should restrict a client from trading beyond a defined margin limit in any segment or across combined derivatives, even if sufficient margin is available.

*Combined derivatives segment includes equity derivatives, currency, and commodity.[ Required same for SLBM Exchange ]*



*Required Separate Fund allocation for SLBM exchange. based on Cash allocation for Equity segment.*

For example, 

If a client has ₹15 lakh in cash balance and ₹20 lakh in collateral margin (total ₹35 lakh margin), we want to cap client’s trading limit in F&O segment at ₹25 lakh. This cap should include margin charged on expiry positions as well. Accordingly, client should not be allowed to trade in the F&O segment beyond ₹25 lakh, even if additional free margin is available.

Similarly, such margin capping control should also be applicable for combined derivatives across all segments (equity derivatives, currency, and commodity).

*Note :* 

{color:#bf2600}No intraday MTM profit benefit will be given, but MTM losses will be considered for margin calculation, and system should work accordingly.{color}

{color:#bf2600}For Options CFS, System should follow exchange rules and allow benefits only for options buy positions within same segment.{color}

{color:#bf2600}For Equity CFS, system should work as per the available system settings.{color}

*Configuration :* 

In fund settings, provide a column to define segment-wise limits for Cash and Futures. System should restrict order placement beyond set limit. 

Currently, we have a cash balance column where a single limit is defined across all exchanges.

* *Impact:* This discrepancy may cause inconsistencies in RMS limit enforcement across segments.

column41:
{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
Please note that the below functionality should only be enabled if the {color:#ff991f}SAFER_PARTICIPATION_API=TRUE{color}
if SAFER_PARTICIPATION_API=FALSE or if the flag is missing, the existing functionality should continue to work flawlessly.
{panel}

h4. *1. Scope*

This requirement applies to all client *Direct API orders* across *NSE, MCX, and BSE* exchanges.
All orders will be treated as *Algo orders*, and no manual order flow will be supported.

----

h4. *2. NNF ID Structure Update*

* The previously used *“1111…” NNF ID* must be *discontinued and replaced*.
* *Revised NNF ID generation:*
** *NSE & MCX:*
*** NNF ID must be *“4444…” (repeated 12 times)*
*** *13th digit:*
**** {{0}} → NSE
**** {{1}} → MCX
** *BSE:*
*** NNF ID must be *“4444…” (repeated 13 times)*
*** *14th digit:*
**** {{0}}

----

h4. *3. Algo ID Requirement (Mandatory)*

* *Algo ID is compulsory for all orders*, as all orders are categorized as *Algo orders*.

----

h4. *4. Algo ID Logic Based on Order Rate*

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
All values should be available in INI file

API_RATE_LIMIT=10

NSE_ALGO_ID_UPTO_RATE_LIMIT=”99999” // exchange specified 

BSE_ALGO_ID_UPTO_RATE_LIMIT=”9999999999999999” // exchange specified

MCX_ALGO_ID_UPTO_RATE_LIMIT=”TBA” // exchange specified

NCDEX_ALGO_ID_UPTO_RATE_LIMIT=”TBA” // exchange specified

MSCI_ALGO_ID_UPTO_RATE_LIMIT=”TBA” // exchange specified

NSE_ALGO_ID_ABOVE_RATE_LIMIT=”{broker_specified_numeric_value}” // broker specified 

BSE_ALGO_ID_ABOVE_RATE_LIMIT=”{broker_specified_numeric_value}” // broker specified

MCX_ALGO_ID_ABOVE_RATE_LIMIT=”{broker_specified_numeric_value}” // broker specified

NCDEX_ALGO_ID_ABOVE_RATE_LIMIT=”{broker_specified_numeric_value}” // broker specified

MSCI_ALGO_ID_ABOVE_RATE_LIMIT=”{broker_specified_numeric_value}” // broker specified
{panel}

* *For NSE:*
** If *order rate ≤ 10 orders/second*
→ Use Algo ID: {{"99999"}}
** If *order rate > 10 orders/second*
→ Use *client-provided Algo ID*
* *For BSE:*
** If *order rate ≤ 10 orders/second*
→ Use Algo ID: {{"9999999999999999"}} (16 times '9')
** If *order rate > 10 orders/second*
→ Use *client-provided Algo ID*



Note: Generic Algo ID for MCX will be updated soon. As of now we are only doing this for normal algo orders through client API. Future plans will include DMA orders through API for which the first 12/13 digits will be 2. Also, we are not sending SOR or inter exchange orders through API so 2 and 4 in the 13th/14th digit is not being included as of now.



{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
Update {{2026-03-04}}

When {color:#ff991f}SAFER_PARTICIPATION_API=TRUE{color}, 

* If {Exchange}_ALGO_ID_{color:#4c9aff}ABOVE{color}_RATE_LIMIT is set, 
** All {Exchange} orders will follow the [Order Rate > API_RATE_LIMIT] scheme and all {Exchange} order will use the {Exchange}_ALGO_ID_{color:#4c9aff}ABOVE{color}_RATE_LIMIT value as the Algo ID for the orders.
* If {Exchange}_ALGO_ID_{color:#4c9aff}ABOVE{color}_RATE_LIMIT is NOT set, 
** All {Exchange} orders will follow the [Order Rate <= API_RATE_LIMIT] scheme and all {Exchange} order will use the {Exchange}_ALGO_ID_{color:#4c9aff}UPTO{color}_RATE_LIMIT value as the Algo ID for the orders. Additionally, all orders above API_RATE_LIMIT will be rejected during that time slice.
{panel}

column495:
09/Apr/26 11:58 AM;712020:2bf45437-71cc-46f5-acad-f438d576a61b;* When an automated order was placed during the market close session, it caused *memory corruption*, due to which *NSEInteractive was crashing when the market opened*. As a result, the remaining orders were not getting processed. This issue has now been resolved.
* This was happening because, during offline order processing, memory was being allocated using {{new}}, which led to the crash. To fix this, we are now assigning the *existing address*  (Shared Memory Buffer received from GATS ) to {{objOfflineQueueInfo.pcGreekData}}.
* Currently, we are testing the same scenario in *BSE*. If the issue exists there as well, we will resolve it and provide updates accordingly.

column1: Total MTM Calculation Enhancement
column41:
*Requirement: Total MTM Calculation Enhancement*

We need a provision to include a value representing past months’ profit/loss (positive or negative MTM) in Total MTM calculation.

*Details:*

* Total MTM should be calculated as:
*Today’s MTM (from current positions) + Past MTM value*
* The past MTM value will be a single number (positive or negative).
* This value will be uploaded in bulk at regular intervals (e.g., once a month).

column1: Net Position View Enhancement
column41:
Requirement: Net Position View Enhancement

While viewing Net Position , traders/admins are currently able to see both open and squared-up positions. This makes navigation difficult as it involves excessive scrolling.

Proposed Change:

By default, only open positions (non-zero quantity) should be displayed.
An option (checkbox/filter toggle) should be provided to “Show All Positions”, which, when selected, will display both open and squared-up positions.

Important Note:

Even when filter is applied to show only open positions (i.e., quantity ≠ 0), MTM (Mark-to-Market) calculation must include all positions, including squared-up positions.
Filter should affect only display/view, not underlying calculations.

column1: IBT Retailer API Algo orders to have NNF as 444444444444 for NSE, BSE, MCX and NCDEX with the last digit unchanged
column41:
If the AlgoID is positive non-zero or a IBT Retailer order then,

* The order is to be treated as IBT algo order
* NNF should reflect that by sending 1st 12 digits of NNF as 444444444444
** In case of NSE, the 13th digit should be 0 in case of normal algo orders, 2 in case of SOR orders and 4 in case of inter exchange algo orders
** In case of BSE , the 14th digit should be 1 in case of normal algo order, 2 in case of SOR orders and 4 in case of inter exchange algo orders
** In case of MCX, the 13th digit should be 1
** In case of NCDEX, the 13th digit should be (TBA)
* Last two digits should be our vendor code. That is 12 for NSE and 14 for BSE, and our other vendor codes for different exchnages.



Note: As of now we are only doing this for normal algo orders through client API. Future plans will include DMA orders through API for which the first 12/13 digits will be 2. Also, we are not sending SOR or inter exchange orders through API so 2 and 4 in the 13th/14th digit is not being included as of now.

column41:
Enhancing Greek Basket Algo (Ctrl+R) – Addressing Self-Trade and Partial Execution Issues from JM Financial 

*Greek Basket algo (Ctrl+ R)*, we would like to formally request a technical enhancement to resolve critical execution gaps caused by *self-trade rejections*.

*The Issue:*
Currently, when a self-trade error occurs, the algo misses the specific slot and only executes a partial quantity. Because the system does not clearly identify or isolate the rejected quantity, we are unable to accurately execute the remaining balance to complete the slot.

*Proposed Solutions:*
To maintain execution efficiency, we suggest one of the following two options:

# *Auto-Retry Logic:* Configure the algo to automatically re-attempt the rejected partial slot immediately.
# *Recovery Window:* Provide a dedicated UI window that displays rejected slot quantities, allowing us to manually place orders to complete the balance.

Please review the technical feasibility of these options and provide an *estimated timeline* for implementation. This fix is essential for ensuring our basket strategies are fully executed without manual reconciliation errors.

column1: Enable Direct Synthetic Order Placement from Watch list
column41:
Introduce functionality to place *Synthetic Orders directly from the Watchlist* by selecting a dedicated market segment ({{SYN}}). The system should auto-configure instrument settings, allow parameter selection, and enable quick order placement via shortcut keys (F1/F2) for long and short synthetic strategies.

----

h3. *Functional Requirements:*

h4. *1. Market Segment & Instrument Selection*

* Add new Market Segment: {{SYN}}
* On selecting {{SYN}}:
** Instrument should be *auto-selected as Synthetic*
** *Option Type field should be disabled/not visible*
* User can select:
** Symbol
** Expiry
** Strike Price

----

h4. *2. Synthetic Pair Loading*

* System should automatically load:
** Corresponding *Call (CE)*
** Corresponding *Put (PE)*
* Pair should be derived based on selected:
** Symbol
** Expiry
** Strike

----

h4. *3. Long Synthetic Order (F1 Key)*

* On pressing *F1*:
** Trigger *Long Synthetic Order*
** Open *2 order windows (Blue color)*:
*** One for *Call (CE)*
*** One for *Put (PE)*
* *Pricing Formula:*
{noformat}Synthetic Price = Strike + Call Ask - Put Bid{noformat}
* *Order Behavior:*
** Orders placed based on above formula
** All other parameters should remain as other normal orders/default setting.
** Allowed Order Types:
*** IOC
*** DAY

----

h4. *4. Short Synthetic Order (F2 Key)*

* On pressing *F2*:
** Trigger *Short Synthetic Order*
** Open *2 order windows (Red color)*:
*** One for *Call (CE)*
*** One for *Put (PE)*
* *Pricing Formula:*
{noformat}Synthetic Price = Strike + Call Bid - Put Ask{noformat}
* *Order Behavior:*
** Orders placed based on above formula
** All other parameters should remain as other normal orders/default setting.
** Allowed Order Types:
*** IOC
*** DAY

----

h4. *5. Order Window Behavior*

* Two separate order windows must always appear:
** CE Leg
** PE Leg
* Windows should:
** Reflect calculated synthetic pricing logic
** Retain user-selected configurations from Watchlist2
* *Synchronized Leg Modification:*
Any changes made in the order placement window of either leg (*Call (CE)* or *Put (PE)*) should be *automatically reflected in the counterpart leg* in real-time.
This includes: Quantity, Order Type, Product Type, and other editable fields.

----

column56:
In BSE :- For order storage, we use two data structures at the time of the order request. The *first 100 orders are stored in an array*, and after that, the remaining orders are *stored in a map*.

In this case, Suppose the first 100 orders are stored in an *array*. When we *modify one of these orders*, the same order is also *stored in the map*. Later, when we *cancel the order*, it gets *removed from the map*, but it is still *present in the array*

Because of this, after the *market opened*, those orders were *sent to the exchange*, and we received *confirmations for those orders*.

This issue has now been *fixed*, and the changes have been *tested successfully*.;14/Mar/26 11:20 AM;712020:2bf45437-71cc-46f5-acad-f438d576a61b;14400

column1: Application of Algorithm Trading Identifier in MSEI
column41:
Apart from Strategy ID, we need to send Strategy trigger Sequence Number (STSN) to exchange. This needs to be done for all type of orders (entry, modification & cancellation)(New STSN for each type of order).

The format of STSN should be dddNNNNNnnnnnnnnn; where 

* ddd denotes the Day of year. In case if day of year is 1 then, '001' needs to be entered. Example 1st January will be “001”, 2nd January will be “002” and so on.
* 'NNNNN' is Number stored by third party applications for product specific strategy. Max range of Strategy ID that can be allocated to any Algo Strategy would be 32000. As of now we have to send “00001” as per direction from exchange.
*  Small n's are running sequence numbers that should be incremented with every request. Thus, the first part dddNNNNN shall represent user defined strategies for a particular day of the year. Each time there is need of sending entry or modification or cancellation request to exchange, third party application is expected to generate new STSN.

The STSN should also be stored with relevant values of Trigger /Opportunity (Say member strategy is 'Sync near month prices to far month' then for each of the order entry / modification / cancellation for far month, member should send STSN and also store values of near month prices against each STSN and values defined by user also i.e. spread).
Third party applications should also have the provision for complete audit trail of values defined by user against a strategy. As part of exchange inspection/system audit, this data will be verified with actual orders and values sent.



The detailed document is attached below for reference.

column1: Inclusion of Delivery Margin in MCX Margin Calculation
column41:
*Inclusion of Delivery Margin in MCX Margin Calculation*

*Current System Calculation:*
*Total Margin = Span + Exposure × (Tender + ELM)%*

Example (Copper Contract):

* Span Margin: 405,000
* Exposure Margin (Tender + ELM = 16.68% + 1.25%)
* Exposure Value: 540,342

*Total Margin (Current as per Greek):*
405,000 + 540,342 = *945,342*

*Proposed Calculation (Including Delivery Margin):*
Delivery Margin (25%) provided by exchange through Daily Margin file needs to be added.

*Revised Formula:*
*Total Margin = Span + Exposure × (Tender + ELM + Delivery Margin)%*

Example (Copper Contract):

* Span Margin: 405,000
* Exposure Margin (16.68% + 1.25% + 25%)
* Exposure Value: 1,293,749

*Total Margin (Revised):*
405,000 + 1,293,749 = *1,699,685*

This update should be applied to all respective MCX contracts. The above copper example is provided for reference.

column494:
26/Feb/26 2:14 PM;712020:846c7254-f2e4-49d9-b665-cf440e06cbf2;After analysis clients RMS tracker file found that

The user initially holds NIFTY 25400 CE Buy – 130 Qty and has a NIFTY 25500 CE Sell order pending. At that time, a SPAN credit of (211.50) in portfolio.(user untick span credit then it not display in margin tab)

After that, the user places a NIFTY 25400 CE Sell – 65 Qty square-off order (pending). At this point, SPAN margin of ₹98.00 is charged and displayed in the RMS Dashboard.

At that time, the margin breakdown is as follows:

SPAN Margin: ₹98.00
Exposure Margin: ₹66,853.80
Option Buy Premium: ₹5,066.75
MTM Loss: ₹1,131.00

Total Exhausted Amount:
98 + 66,853.80 + 5,066.75 + 1,131 = ₹73,149.71

The user then places another NIFTY 25400 CE Sell – remaining 65 Qty square-off order. However, once this order is placed, the SPAN margin for the pending NIFTY 25500 CE Sell order increases to ₹169,690.50 as per the portfolio.

Due to this margin increase, the user receives a Fund Rejection message:
"Not enough deposit available Allowed Fund: 104133.94 Exceeded by: 138608.57 Exhausted: 73149.71 MtoM: -1131.00 Allowed OptSellCredit: 0.00 Exhausted OptSellCredit: 0.00.| [NSE] [NIFTY 24FEB26 CE 25400] SELL 65 @ 48.4000"

Margin Calculation at the Time of Second Sell Order (65 Qty)

SPAN Margin (NIFTY 25500 CE Sell pending): ₹169,690.50
Exposure Margin: ₹66,853.80
Remaining 25400 CE Buy 65 Qty – Option Premium: ₹5,066.75
MTM Loss: ₹1,131.00

Total Margin Required:
169,690.50 + 66,853.80 + 5,066.75 + 1,131 = ₹242,742.51

Available (Allowed) Fund: ₹104,133.94

Shortfall (Exceeded Amount):
104,133.94 – 242,742.51 = ₹138,608.57

Therefore, the order is rejected due to insufficient available funds, as the total required margin exceeds the allowed fund balance.

column1: Physical Margin need to charge dynamically
column41:
Physical Margin need to charge dynamically

h3. Dynamic Charging of Physical (Delivery) Margin for Options

*Current Behavior:*

* Delivery margin is currently charged only on options marked *ITM* in the contract file at the start of the day.

*Required Behavior (As per Exchange Logic):*

* *Dynamic Margin Application:*
** If an option becomes *ITM* during trading day → delivery margin should be applied immediately.
** If an option moves *out of ITM* during the trading day → delivery margin should be revoked for that particular record.

*Example:*

* Suppose *Reliance 1400 CE* is initially ITM in the contract file.
* Then delivery margin should be applied
* During market session, if the stock price moves such that *1400 CE becomes OTM*, the system should automatically *revoke the delivery margin* charged for this option.

column1: “In The Money (ITM)” Column in Market Watch
column41:
24-02-2026 (Update)

h3. Settings Dependency (Important)

* ITM calculation must be aligned with *Option Calculator settings configured by the client*.
* For example: If option calculations are set to *Synthetic basis*, then synthetic underlying price must be used instead of spot CMP.
* Any other pricing basis or adjustments configured in Option Calculator (e.g., underlying selection, premium basis, etc.) must be used for calculation.
* The ITM value in Market Watch must dynamically reflect the *same calculation logic and settings* currently applied in Option Calculator.





Add values to the column named *“In The Money”* in the Market Watch section to display the intrinsic value of option contracts (Call/Put). For all non-option instruments, this column will remain blank.

----

h3. Calculation Logic

Let:

* *Strike Price (K)* = Option Strike Price
* *CMP (S)* = Current Market Price of Underlying

h4. 1️⃣ Call Option

*Formula:*
ITM Value = CMP – Strike Price (S – K)

*Cases:*

* If S > K → Positive value → Call is *In The Money*
* If S = K → 0 → At The Money
* If S < K → Negative value → Out of The Money

*Example:*

* Call Strike = 1500
* CMP = 1400
* ITM = 1400 – 1500 = *-100*

----

h4. 2️⃣ Put Option

*Formula:*
ITM Value = Strike Price – CMP (K – S)

*Cases:*

* If K > S → Positive value → Put is *In The Money*
* If K = S → 0 → At The Money
* If K < S → Negative value → Out of The Money

*Example:*

* Put Strike = 1500
* CMP = 1400
* ITM = 1500 – 1400 = *+100*

----

h3. Display Rules

* Column Name: *In The Money*
* Applicable only for *Options (Call/Put)*
* For Equity, Futures, Currency, Commodity, or any non-option instrument → *Column remains blank*
* Value should update dynamically with CMP changes.

column1: Calendar Spread margin benefit for Single Stock Derivatives on expiry day
column41:
Calendar Spread margin benefit for Single Stock Derivatives on expiry day

We draw your attention to SEBI circular ref. no. HO/47/15/11(2)2025-MRD-TPD1/ I/4226/2026 dated February 05, 2026, and NCL circular ref. no. 018/2026 (Download ref. no. NCL/CMPT/72659) dated February 05, 2026, regarding Calendar Spread margin benefit for Single Stock Derivatives on expiry day.

SPAN Margin
•
The existing tag called ‘scanTiers’ in .spn file shall be used.
o
For stock symbols, on the day of expiry there shall be two tiers under ‘scanTiers’ tag.
▪
Tier 1 shall contain the nearest expiry (T Date) for both starting and ending period.
▪
Tier 2 shall contain the next expiry and the farthest expiry respectively in the starting and ending period.
o
On non-expiry days, for stock symbols there shall be one tier containing the nearest and farthest expiry respectively in the starting and ending period.
o
You may refer the span tags provided in Annexure to NCL Circular ref. no. 146/2024 (Download ref. no. NCL/CMPT/65314) dated November 29, 2024.
•
On expiry day for a stock, tag ‘dspread’ shall not contain any combination of expiries with the nearest expiry date (T Date).



Extreme Loss Margin
In case of calendar spread positions in future contracts, the stock futures positions in expiry day contracts shall not be granted calendar spread treatment on the day of expiry. Such stock positions in expiry day contracts shall not be considered from start of expiry day whereby no calendar spread benefit in Extreme Loss Margins shall be available on such stock futures positions.
The circular shall come into effect from May 04, 2026.

* On expiry day:

When an order is placed in the NSE-FO pre-open session, it initially goes into the *Pending* state. However, after modifying the same order, it was moving to the *Unconfirmed* state because the {{iPreOpenAllowed}} value was not set in the ScriptDesc map. Here we will list all masters, SQLs or programs to fetch data and data synchronization between Main system and GNexLayer Middleware. 

Considering multitenant (multibroker) hosting on GNexLayer all generated files will have to be in respective buckets of MINIO as identified by broker tags viewed on Brokers onboarding screen.

# ProductMaster.csv ({{productmaster }})

# RMSExpenseMaster.csv ({{rmsexpensemaster}})
# BrokerContractMapping.csv ({{contracts}})

$ export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$LD_LIBRARY_PATH:/usr/local/lib64:/usr/local/lib   //To be executed only once or in new terminal session

$ ./XChangeFileDownloader.out

    ud.HIDE_SHOW_SQUAREOFFPOSI AS HIDE_SHOW_SQUAREOFFPOSI ,
    ud.OPTSTR_VALUE AS OPTSTR_VALUE,
    ud.OPTSTR_VALUE_BUILDER AS OPTSTR_VALUE_BUILDER,
    btm.cTemplateName AS cTemplateName,
    CONCAT_WS(
        ',',
        CASE WHEN crp.deliveryproductsetting = true THEN deliveryProduct ELSE NULL END,
        CASE WHEN crp.intradayproductsetting = true THEN intradayProduct ELSE NULL END,
        CASE WHEN crp.bmtf = true THEN mtfProduct ELSE NULL END,
        CASE WHEN crp.btncproduct = true THEN tncProduct ELSE NULL END,
        CASE WHEN crp.bcoverproduct = true THEN catalystProduct ELSE NULL END,
        CASE WHEN crp.bsseq = true THEN sseqProduct ELSE NULL END
    ) AS AllowedProducts
FROM clientdetails cd
INNER JOIN clients c
    ON cd.cgreekuserorinvestorid = c.gscid
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT gscid, password, pass_type
    FROM authinfo
    WHERE pass_type = 3
      AND gscid = cd.cgreekuserorinvestorid
    ORDER BY last_updated_time DESC
    LIMIT 1
) ai ON TRUE
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        a.gscid,
        string_agg(a.password, ',' ORDER BY a.last_updated_time) AS previousmpins
    FROM authinfo a
    JOIN (
        SELECT
            gscid,
            MAX(last_updated_time) AS latest_time
        FROM authinfo
        WHERE pass_type = 3
        GROUP BY gscid
    ) b
        ON a.gscid = b.gscid
    WHERE a.pass_type = 3
      AND a.last_updated_time < b.latest_time
    GROUP BY a.gscid
) aipp
    ON cd.cgreekuserorinvestorid = aipp.gscid
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        gscid,
        MAX(CASE WHEN datakey = 'ThemeSettings' THEN data END) AS ThemeSettings,
        MAX(CASE WHEN datakey = 'ColumnProfile' THEN data END) AS ColumnProfile,
        MAX(CASE WHEN datakey = 'holdingFilter' THEN data END) AS holdingFilter,
        MAX(CASE WHEN datakey = 'watchlistExchFilter' THEN data END) AS watchlistExchFilter,
        MAX(CASE WHEN datakey = 'watchlistFilter' THEN data END) AS watchlistFilter,
        MAX(CASE WHEN datakey = 'HIDE_SHOW_SQUAREOFFPOSI' THEN data END) AS HIDE_SHOW_SQUAREOFFPOSI,
        MAX(CASE WHEN datakey = 'OPTSTR_VALUE' THEN data END) AS OPTSTR_VALUE,
        MAX(CASE WHEN datakey = 'OPTSTR_VALUE_BUILDER' THEN data END) AS OPTSTR_VALUE_BUILDER
    FROM userdata
    GROUP BY gscid
) ud
    ON cd.cgreekUserorinvestorid = ud.gscid
LEFT JOIN brokeragetemplatemapper btm
    ON cd.cgreekuserorinvestorid = btm.cretailerid
LEFT JOIN clientriskpreference crp
    ON cd.cgreekuserorinvestorid = crp.cuser
   AND crp.cusercategory = 'Retailer'
WHERE
    cd.ccategory = 'Retail'
    AND cd.bisibt = 1;
END $$;{noformat}

05/Mar/26 11:12 AM;712020:c559aac8-af4e-4a0d-a62d-565237c8817e;Test cases For Holding in RMS_AdvanceBuyBack=true scenario

Full Square Off (Holding):
→ Sell full holding quantity → Expected: Position becomes zero and P&L calculated correctly.

Product Change After Full Square Off:
→ Change product after full square off → Expected: Product change not allowed as no position exists.

Partial Square Off (Holding):
→ Sell partial holding quantity → Expected: Remaining holding quantity reduces correctly.

Product Change After Partial Square Off:
→ Try product change after partial sell → Expected: Product change allowed only for sold quantity.

Extra Buy + Partial Sell:
→ Buy extra quantity then sell partial → Expected: Holdings  reduces as per soldl quantity.

Product Change After Extra Buy + Partial Sell:
→ Change product after extra buy and partial sell → Expected: Product change allowed only for open net quantity.

Extra Buy + Full Square Off:
→ Buy extra then sell total (holding + extra) → Expected: Net position becomes zero.

Extra Buy + Extra Sell:
→ Buy extra and sell more than holding but within total qty → Expected: Position adjusts correctly without rejection.

Sell More Than Holding:
→ Sell quantity greater than available holding → Expected: Order rejected or converted as per RMS rules.

Holding Sell and Buyback:
→ Sell holding and buy same quantity again → Expected: Position restored and treated as new holding if intraday closed.

Partial Product Change after Holding Sell:
→ Sell partial holding and change product  → Expected: Product change allowed only for sold qty.

Today’s Delivery Netposition Impact:
→ Buy today as delivery and check net position → Expected: Net position reflects today's delivery correctly with holding.

We have introduced a new configuration flag {{F7NetBackOfficeCode}} in Trading Style settings.

h3. *Changes Implemented:*

# *New Global Variable Added*
#* Added:
{noformat}std::string AppGlobal::strF7netBackOfficeCode = "";
{noformat}
#* When {{F7NetBackOfficeCode}} is set in trading style, its value is assigned to:
{noformat}AppGlobal::strF7netBackOfficeCode
{noformat}
# *Impact on SPL Export (Special Format Export Only)*
The following behavior changes apply *only during SPL format export*:
1.) Client Code Override
#* If {{AppGlobal::strF7netBackOfficeCode}} is *NOT empty*:
#** The exported *Client Code* will be replaced with the configured {{F7NetBackOfficeCode}} value.
#* If empty:
#** System behaves as earlier (uses grid Client Code).
# 2.) Realized PnL Export
#* If:
#** {{F7NetBackOfficeCode}} is set, AND
#** {{NetQty == 0}}
#* Then:
#** Net PnL is calculated from {{NETAMT}}
#** Sign is inverted
#** Exported in the last column (previously Realized IV field position)
# 3.) Futures Handling
#* If the security is identified as *Future* ({{StrikePrice <= 0}}):
#** {{CashType = "FU"}}
#** If {{F7NetBackOfficeCode}} is set:
#*** {{OptionType}} is forced to {{"FX"}}
# *No Impact Areas*
#* No changes in:
#** Normal display
#** Other exports
#** Calculations
#* Change is strictly limited to *SPL format export flow*





h3. *Summary of Functional Behavior*

||Condition||Behavior||
|{{F7NetBackOfficeCode}} empty|Existing behavior retained|
|{{F7NetBackOfficeCode}} set|Client Code overridden in export|
|NetQty = 0 & flag set|Realized PnL exported|
|Future & flag set|OptionType exported as {{FX}}|

column1: Stock Alert : Alert Trigger When LTP Reaches User-Defined Price
column41:
h3. Description

The system shall allow users to set a price alert for any selected script. An alert shall be triggered when the script’s Last Traded Price (LTP) reaches the user-defined target price.

h3. Functional Requirements

# The system shall allow the user to select a script from the available market instruments.
# The system shall allow the user to specify a target price for the selected script.
# The system shall continuously monitor the LTP of the selected script.
# The system shall trigger an alert when the LTP *equals* the user-defined target price.
# Provide a time base alert setting when the target price matched more than once in very less time so that the multiple popups can be ignored and other popup will generate upon reaching the time mentioned.

h3. Non-Functional Requirements

* The alert trigger latency shall not exceed acceptable market data delay thresholds.
* The system shall support multiple active price alerts per user.
* The system shall handle concurrent alerts without performance degradation.

h3. Assumptions

* Real-time or near real-time market data for LTP is available.
* User has permission to view the selected script.

h3. Acceptance Criteria

* Given a script and a target price are set,
When the LTP reaches the specified price,
Then the system triggers an alert to the user.
* The alert is not retriggered unless the alert is reset or edited.

column1: XDP Module in Transport
column41:
*XDP (eXpress Data Path)* is a high-performance packet processing framework in the Linux kernel that allows you to run custom eBPF programs at the earliest point in the network stack — right in the NIC driver — before the kernel allocates socket buffers. This enables ultra-low-latency packet filtering, redirection, and modification.

XDP programs are written in restricted C, compiled to eBPF bytecode, verified for safety, and JIT-compiled in the kernel for execution.

column1: Update child order FIX responses to reflect parent order execution status
column41:
h2. Current Behavior

* When a *parent order* is split into multiple *child orders*, each child order is traded independently.
* If a *child order is fully executed*, the system sends a *child leg response* with:
** *Tag 39 = 2 (Filled)* — indicating that specific child order is fully traded.
* Even if one or more child orders are fully filled, the *parent order* may still be *partially executed* if other child orders remain open.
** In this case, the *head (parent) response* reflects:
*** *Tag 39 = 1 (Partially Filled)*.
* Once *all child orders are fully executed* and the total parent quantity is filled:
** The *head response of the last child order* is updated to:
*** *Tag 39 = 2 (Filled)* — indicating the parent order is now fully traded.

----

h2. *Required Change*

* When a *child order is partially filled*, either:
** *slice-wise*, or
** *cumulatively less than the child order quantity*,
* the system *must send the child leg response with*:
** *Tag 39 = 1 (Partially Filled)*.
* *Tag 39 = 2 (Filled)* for a leg response *must only be sent when the entire  order quantity is fully executed*, not for any intermediate slice-level executions.

----

h2. *Expected Tag 39 Behavior Summary*

||Order Level||Execution State||Tag 39||
|Child Leg|Slice-wise / partial execution|1|
|Child Leg|Fully executed (child quantity filled)|2|
|Parent|One or more child orders pending|1|
|Parent|All child orders fully executed|2|

column1: FixRMS: User Defined Quantity Limit as % of Issued Capital
column41:
*Description:* Restrict total order quantity based on a user-defined percentage of the instrument’s issued capital.

*Requirement Details:*

* Provide a configurable *Issued Capital % Limit* field in FIX RMS.
* User will input a percentage value.
* System to fetch issued capital for the instrument.
* Maximum allowable cumulative order quantity should be calculated as:
{{Issued Capital × User Defined Percentage}}

*Example:*

* Issued Capital = 300,000
* User Input = 1%
* Max Allowed Quantity = 3,000
* Any order resulting in cumulative quantity above 3,000 should be *rejected*.

column1: FixRMS: Total Single Order Quantity as % of Average Daily Volume (ADV)
column41:
*Description:* Restrict total order quantity based on a user-defined percentage of the instrument’s Average Daily Volume (ADV).

*Requirement Details:*

* Provide a configurable *ADV % Limit* field in FIX RMS.
* User will input a percentage value (e.g., 10%).
* System to fetch/calculate Average Daily Volume for the instrument.
* Maximum allowable cumulative order quantity should be calculated as:
{{ADV × User Defined Percentage}}

*Example:*

* ADV = 100,000
* User Input = 10%
* Max Allowed Quantity = 10,000
* Orders exceeding cumulative quantity of 10,000 should be *rejected*.

*Description:* Restrict total order value placed by a user/algo such that it does not exceed a user-defined turnover limit.

*Requirement Details:*

* A configurable *Turnover Limit* field to be provided in FIX RMS.
* User will input the maximum allowed turnover value.

column496:
20/Feb/26 6:44 PM;712020:0881dd6c-72db-4ddd-ac3c-e46e156a485c;The issue occurred because the *OrderInfo* table was deleted, and the user restarted the server component. As a result, when we tried to log in to the exchange, the trade data was downloaded, but we weren't able to retrieve the *LourOrderNo* for Algo orders, so it was set to 0.

In our system, we assign the *LourOrderNo* to downloaded trades using the *iMessageTag* field from the *TradeNotification* exchange structure. We populate this field with the *LourOrderNo* when sending the Order Entry request to the exchange, and the *LourOrderNo* comes back in the Order Response as a reference.

The problem happened with *Algo orders* because the Order Entry request structure for Algo orders does not contain the *iMessageTag* field or any similar field. To manage this, we typically rely on the *OrderInfo* table.

To resolve this, we made changes to get the *LourOrderNo* from the *TradeInfo* table instead.

However, in *Zero Downloading functionality*, when we download all orders and trades, we don’t receive the *LourOrderNo* for Algo orders, which is why it’s being set to 0 for these orders. This issue only affects *Algo orders*.

Description :- 

h3. Requirement Description: Price Deviation Control for FIX Orders

The system shall provide a configurable *price deviation control mechanism* for FIX orders to manage execution risk and ensure dealer awareness before order acknowledgment and execution.

h4. 1. Pre-Acknowledgement Price Deviation Check

* The user shall be able to define a *percentage price limit* for FIX orders via *FIX RMS or an equivalent configuration window*.
* When a FIX order is received, the system shall compare the *order price* against the reference price (e.g., LTP or market reference price).
* If the order price deviates beyond the configured threshold (e.g., *2%*):
** A *pop-up alert* shall be displayed to the dealer *within the FIX order window before order acknowledgement*.
** The pop-up shall clearly describe:
*** Order price
*** Reference price
*** Percentage deviation
*** Configured limit
** The dealer shall be provided with options to:
*** *Accept* the order and proceed with acknowledgement, or
*** *Reject* the order.
* The order shall not be acknowledged until the dealer takes an explicit action.

----

h4. 2. Post-Acceptance Execution Deviation Check

* The system shall support a second, *user-defined percentage threshold* (e.g., *10%*) for monitoring price movement after the order has been accepted.
* Once an order is accepted, the system shall continuously monitor the *Last Traded Price (LTP)* of the instrument.
* If the LTP moves beyond the configured post-acceptance threshold relative to the *original accepted order price*:
** A *pop-up alert* shall be triggered for the dealer.
** The pop-up shall provide options to:
*** *Continue* further execution of the order, or
*** *Stop/Halt* further execution.
* Dealer action shall be mandatory, and execution behavior shall follow the selected option.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
Point 2 is to be carved out into a separate requirement and parked for now.
{panel}

----

h4. 3. Configuration & Control

* Both percentage thresholds (pre-acknowledgement and post-acceptance) shall be:
** *User-configurable*
** Controlled via *FIX RMS or an approved configuration interface*
* The feature shall support different settings per:
** User / dealer
** Instrument / segment (if applicable)

----

h4. 4. Audit & Compliance

* All pop-up triggers and dealer actions (accept, reject, continue, stop) shall be:
** Time-stamped
** Logged for audit and compliance purposes
