column1: Send historical data of TER to client on Subscription. and Batch Update of TER in DB.
column41:
* When a client subscribes to a token, historical TER information is also sent to the client. If the client subscribes to a single token, the data for that token will be sent in a single-token structure.  If the client subscribes to a portfolio, historical TER information will be sent in an array of 25 tokens (existing structure). For BCAST 2, historical data is sent to the client in an array of 25 tokens, whether the client subscribes to a single token or a portfolio,  to avoid structure changes on the client - server side .
* Currently, TER Broadcasts are sent in batches of 25 tokens at a time. 
* *OPTIMIZATION REQUIRED:*
*  In the future, we plan to optimize the batch size of 25 tokens to a value suitable for our TCP buffer. However, this optimization is on hold for now to avoid changes to the compatibility number. This change will be implemented in the Optimus release or another development release, as per management’s decision.(Please refer below sub task for this changes GETSCTCL-13730) 
* We will also implement the following optimization in future: TER Broadcast will be sent to clients on a subscription basis. Currently, TER Broadcasts were sent to all clients without checking whether they had subscribed. TER Broadcasts are received in bulk from exchange (maximum 25 tokens). If a client has subscribed to any one of the 25 tokens, the broadcast packet will be sent to that client.


*Please take updated patch of client, server side for this changes.*

column1: Dissemination of indices in CM and F&O Segment "Nifty India Railways PSU" and "Nifty Conglomerate 50"
column41:
1. Across all exchanges, when a new index is introduced (received via broadcast), the system will automatically generate an index code. A CSV file will be created to store index names and their corresponding index codes. All index details will be loaded from this CSV file in the application. If the CSV file is not found, the system will continue to operate using the currently exiting coding . If a new index is detected in the broadcast feed, the system will automatically create and assign a new index code to the corresponding index name and update the CSV file accordingly. For synchronization of index codes across all servers and different client-side applications (for GMBS and non-CTCL projects), it is sufficient to share this CSV file containing the index details (index name and index code).



h3. Existing Flow

# Index Name and Index Code are hardcoded in the application.
# The system syncs this data with the *indexmaster* table.
# If a new index is comes, it is automatically inserted into the database with minimum indexcode.

h3. New Flow

# First checks if *indexinfo.csv* file exists or not.
# If *indexinfo.csv exists*:
#* Index Name and Index Code are read from the CSV file.
#* The system syncs this data with the *indexmaster* table.
# If *indexinfo.csv does not exist*:
#* The system uses hardcoded Index Name and Index Code.
#* It creates *indexinfo.csv* file and insert data into file..
#* The system syncs this data with the *indexmaster* database table.

h3. 

{color:#ff5630}*! Note* {color}*: The indexinfo.csv file should be placed with ini file during server setup*

----

# Following are Exchange changes

The Exchange proposes online dissemination of the following indices on trading system w.e.f. February 09, 2026.

The values of indices shall be provided in index broadcast window (top right corner) and in multiple index broadcast screen in NEAT+ with the following broadcast name.

 

|Sr. No.|Index Name|Broadcast Name|
|1|Nifty India Railways PSU|Nifty RailwaysPSU|
|2|Nifty Conglomerate 50|NiftyConglomerate|

 

 

Members using Non-Neat Front end (NNF) can configure/develop their system to receive the index broadcast. The factsheet of the indices are provided as Annexure.

Additional information regarding above mentioned indices is available on Exchange website in following path:-

 

|*Sr. No.*|*Index Name*|*NSE India Link*|
|1|Nifty India Railways PSU|[https://www.nseindia.com/static/products-services/indices-thematic|https://www.nseindia.com/static/products-services/indices-thematic|smart-link]|
|2|Nifty Conglomerate 50|[https://www.nseindia.com/static/products-services/indices-thematic|https://www.nseindia.com/static/products-services/indices-thematic|smart-link]|

 

Further, the Exchange shall provide the details of above-mentioned indices in market indices report (.in & .id files) broadcast to the local database of terminals, end of day press files and market activity report available on Exchange website and extranet.

column1: Funds and Margin Data model: Database table structures for Funds and Margins
column41:
GETS Managers backend OMS/RMS has categorized segments in three categories:

# Cash and derivatives are clubbed together in non-commodity(value as “0”) segment, 
# commodity (value=1) segment and 
# currency(value=2) segment are treated separately.

Code snippet/#defines are given below just for reference:

{noformat}
#define MARGIN_NON_COMMODITY_INDEX  0
#define MARGIN_COMMODITY_INDEX      1
#define MARGIN_CURRENCY_INDEX       2
#define MARGIN_MAX_INDEX            3{noformat}

Products allowed:

{noformat}#define PRODUCT_DELIVERY		0
#define PRODUCT_INTRADAY		1
#define PRODUCT_MTF			    2
#define PRODUCT_TNC			    3
#define PRODUCT_COVER			4

#define MAX_PRODUCTS_ALLOWED	5{noformat}



For reference:

{noformat}enum MARGIN_SEGMENT
{
        ALL=0,
        COMMODITY=1,
        NON_COMMODITY=2
};{noformat}



Tables and Views to store Funds and Margins(EQ and FO):



*//Table*

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS userfunddetails(
        ibrokerid integer,
        strbrokertag text COLLATE pg_catalog."default",
        strgscid char(21) not NULL DEFAULT ' ', 
        igcid integer,     
        imktseg  integer,   
        ffundavailable  real DEFAULT 0,
        fpayinamt  real DEFAULT 0,
        fpayoutamt  real DEFAULT 0,
        fmtf  real DEFAULT 0,		
        lastupdatedtime BIGINT not NULL,
        strupdatedby text COLLATE pg_catalog."default" NOT NULL DEFAULT ''::text,

        CONSTRAINT pk_userfunddetails PRIMARY KEY (strgscid, imktseg)
);



//View

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW view_userfundsummary AS 
SELECT 
    strgscid, SUM(ffundavailable) AS total_ffundavailable, SUM(fpayoutamt) AS total_fpayoutamt,  SUM(fpayinamt)  AS total_fpayinamtt,  SUM(fmtf)  AS total_fmtf  
FROM userfunddetails 
GROUP BY strgscid; 

//Sample select statement on view:

select * from view_userfundsummary  where cgreekclientid='GSC001' and imktseg = 0 ;



//Segment: 0

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS userfomargin(
        ibrokerid integer,
        strbrokertag text COLLATE pg_catalog."default",
        strgscid char(21) not NULL DEFAULT ' ', 
        igcid integer,     
        imktseg  integer,   
	iproducttype  integer, 
        foptsellcredit  real DEFAULT 0, 
        foptbuyprem  real DEFAULT 0, 
        fspan  real DEFAULT 0, 
        fexpos  real DEFAULT 0 , 		
        lastupdatedtime BIGINT not NULL, 
        strupdatedby text COLLATE pg_catalog."default" NOT NULL DEFAULT ''::text, 

        CONSTRAINT pk_userfomargin  PRIMARY KEY (strgscid, imktseg, iproducttype)
);

//View

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW view_userfomarginsummary AS 
SELECT 
    strgscid,  SUM(foptsellcredit) AS total_foptsellcredit, SUM(foptbuyprem ) AS total_foptbuyprem , SUM(fspan) AS total_fspan, SUM(fexpos) AS total_fexpos 
FROM userfomargin 
GROUP BY strgscid  ;





//Segment: 0

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS usereqmargin(
        ibrokerid integer,
        strbrokertag text COLLATE pg_catalog."default",
        strgscid  char(21) not NULL DEFAULT ' ', 
        igcid integer,     

        imktseg  integer DEFAULT 2 ,  
	iproducttype  integer, 
        fcashmargin  real DEFAULT 0, 
        fequitysellcredit  real DEFAULT 0, 	
        lastupdatedtime BIGINT not NULL, 
        strupdatedby text COLLATE pg_catalog."default" NOT NULL DEFAULT ''::text, 

        CONSTRAINT pk_usereqmargin  PRIMARY KEY (strgscid, iproducttype) 
);



CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW view_usereqmarginsummary AS 
SELECT 
    strgscid,  SUM(fcashmargin) AS total_fcashmargin, SUM(fequitysellcredit) AS total_fequitysellcredit 
FROM usereqmargin 
GROUP BY strgscid  ;

Orders Cancellation and modification request were rejected multiple times by the exchange with error *“Product ID not found.”* Upon analysis, we identified a *product ID mismatch between the BSE_EQ and CC files provided by the exchange*.

 

Specifically, on *30th January 2026*, in file *BSE_EQD_contract_30012026.csv*, product ID for *Sensex 76000 PE, expiry 5-Feb-2026* is mentioned as *1063*, whereas in *EQD_CC_CO300126.csv*, same contract is reflected with product ID *1064*. 

Also miss match for many other contract

 

We have observed same issue for other clients as well. We had already communicated this to *Trading Operations* team; however, we have not received any response so far.

We kindly request you to *coordinate with the exchange* to address and resolve this discrepancy at the earliest.

column1: MTF Position Quantity Blocking
column41:
*Requirement*
MTF holding positions *must not be allowed to sell on settlement holidays*. System shall provide a *quantity-level block for MTF holdings* to restrict sell quantity on such days.

----

h3. Blocking Logic

* On *settlement holidays*, system shall:
**  Read *MTF holding quantities*
** *Block entire MTF quantity* from sell eligibility
* No partial sell of MTF quantity to be allowed when the quantity is mentioned in the window.

*Example*

* MTF Holding Quantity: 100 shares
* Sellable Quantity for MTF = 0

----

h3. RMS & Greek

* Quantity block must be *visible in RMS window*
* Corresponding changes required in *Greek* to reflect:
** Total MTF quantity
** Blocked MTF quantity
** Sellable quantity = 0

----

h3. Key Conditions

* Blocking is *product-specific (MTF only)*
* Intraday positions not impacted
* Block is removed automatically on next working settlement day

column1: Additional margin blocking
column41:
*Requirement*
System shall support an *Additional Utilization mechanism at BOD*, where a *valid file upload* is required to block client-level funds.

----

h3. Input File (Mandatory at BOD)

*Columns (Only 2):*

# {{Client Code}}
# {{Value}} (Positive number only)

* File can only be upload *at BOD*
* Invalid rows must be rejected with error logs

----

h3. Blocking Logic

* Entered {{Value}} will be *blocked from client’s available funds*
* Block is *independent of margin type* and treated as *hard blocking*
* Block applies *across segments* (final confirmation pending)

*Capping Rule*

* If {{Value}} > Available Funds → *Block only available funds*

*Example*

* Available Funds: ₹1,00,000
* Uploaded Value: ₹10,000 → Block ₹10,000
* Uploaded Value: ₹1,20,000 → Block ₹1,00,000

----

h3. Key Conditions

* Blocking is applied *only at BOD*
* No negative balance allowed
* Latest uploaded value overwrites previous value
* Block remains active until next valid BOD upload

column1: Enable multiple tabs with filter functionality in IOB window similar to Market Watch window
column41:
h3. *Description*

Currently, the IOB window supports only a single view. To enhance usability and align it with the Market Watch window, the IOB window should support *multiple tabs*, where each tab can have *independent filters*.
This will allow clients to monitor and work with different datasets or filter criteria simultaneously across multiple tabs.

----

h3. *Business Requirement*

Clients should be able to:

* Open multiple tabs within the IOB window
* Apply different filters on each tab
* Switch between tabs without losing applied filters or data state
* allow to name the tabs as per requirement
* Provide Maximum Tab settings in IOB Default settings. This will define up to how many tabs a dealer can open.

This improves efficiency, flexibility, and user experience for active traders.

----

h3. *Functional Requirements*

# IOB window should support *multiple tabs*, similar to Market Watch.
# Users should be able to *add, rename, and close tabs*.
# Each tab should support *independent filter configuration*.
# Filters applied in one tab *must not affect* other tabs.
# Tab data and filters should *persist while the session is active*.

----

h3. *Acceptance Criteria*

* Given the user is on the IOB window
When the user adds a new tab
Then a new tab is created with default (no) filters applied
* Given multiple tabs exist
When the user applies a filter on Tab A
Then Tab B remains unaffected
* Given the user switches between tabs
Then the previously applied filters and data state are retained
* Given the user closes a tab
Then only that tab is removed without impacting other tabs

----

h3. *UI/UX Notes*

* Tab behavior and layout should be *consistent with Market Watch window*
* Clear visual indication of the active tab
* Filters should be easily accessible within each tab

----

h3. *Non-Functional Requirements*

* No performance degradation when multiple tabs are open
* Smooth switching between tabs
* Scalability to support multiple tabs (as per system limits)

----

h3. *Dependencies / References*

* Market Watch window tab implementation (for reference and consistency)

22/Jan/26 2:57 PM;6427ece40e6828ab2027c570;[~accountid:63f4afb4c1f7acaf636b80ba] [~accountid:60fea6016051c5006a6eadce]  When the user changes the theme from the settings, the chart screen initially renders using the previous theme and then switches to the new theme after a few milliseconds. This happens only the first time because we are using localStorage in TradingView. Due to this, the old theme is applied briefly before the new theme takes effect. This is a known issue in TradingView as well, and it is documented in the link below.

[https://www.tradingview.com/charting-library-docs/latest/customization/customization-issues/|https://www.tradingview.com/charting-library-docs/latest/customization/customization-issues/|smart-link]

column1: Enhancements related to stop loss orders in Equity Derivatives segment
column41:
Incoming SL-limit order shall be accepted if the difference between trigger price and limit price is less than or equal to the permissible range, else it shall be rejected.

h3. A) Index Futures (FUTIDX)

||Trigger Price||Rule||
|≤ ₹10,000|*Max difference = ₹200 (fixed)*|
|> ₹10,000|*Max difference = 2% of Trigger Price*|

----

h3. B) Index Options (OPTIDX)

||Trigger Price||Rule||
|≤ ₹50|*Max difference = ₹10 (fixed)*|
|> ₹50|*Max difference = 20% of Trigger Price*|

h2.  FUTIDX Examples 

h3. Example 1: Trigger price ≤ 10,000

*Trigger Price:* 9,800
*Permissible Range:* ₹200

||Limit Price||Difference||Result||
|9,850|50|✅ Accepted|
|9,600|200|✅ Accepted|
|9,550|250|“Stop limit order price range check failed”|

----

h3. Example 2: Trigger price > 10,000

*Trigger Price:* 15,000
*Permissible Range:*
2% of 15,000 = *₹300*

||Limit Price||Difference||Result||
|14,800|200|✅ Accepted|
|14,700|300|✅ Accepted|
|14,600|400|“Stop limit order price range check failed”|

----

h2. ✅ OPTIDX Examples (Index Options)

h3. Example 3: Trigger price ≤ 50

*Trigger Price:* 40
*Permissible Range:* ₹10

||Limit Price||Difference||Result||
|38|2|✅ Accepted|
|30|10|✅ Accepted|
|25|15|“Stop limit order price range check failed”|

----

h3. Example 4: Trigger price > 50

*Trigger Price:* 100
*Permissible Range:*
20% of 100 = *₹20*

||Limit Price||Difference||Result||
|95|5|✅ Accepted|
|80|20|✅ Accepted|
|70|30|“Stop limit order price range check failed”|

----

h2. Applies to Order Modification also

This check is applied when:

* Placing *new SL-Limit orders*
* *Modifying* Trigger Price or Limit Price of existing SL-Limit orders

If modification breaks the rule → “Stop limit order price range check failed”





*Go live date for the same is* {{2026-02-09}}*. It shall be available for testing in mock trading session scheduled on Saturday,* {{2026-02-07}}

If Reliance reflects an MTM profit of ₹10,000 and SBIN reflects an MTM loss of ₹8,000, system should net off the positions and consider a net MTM profit of ₹2,000. This net profit should not be added to available funds and should only be used to offset losses on a portfolio-wise basis.

In cases where the net MTM results in a loss, loss amount should be deducted from applicable margin.

column1: Holdings Management and File uploads
column41:
*Holdings* in a trading system refer to the stocks or securities held by an investor, dealer, or broker. In a CTCL (Computer-to-Computer Link) environment, holdings can be updated manually or through files provided by the back office. There are four main types of holdings in a trading system, which are explained below.

*Types of Holdings*

# *Pool Account*: A *pool account* acts as a temporary holding area for securities and funds during the settlement process. Brokers use it to transfer securities to and from the clearing corporation. There are various types of holdings within a pool account:
## *BTST (Buy Today, Sell Tomorrow) Holdings*: These holdings are those that must be compulsorily sold on the next trading day.
# *DP (Demat) Account:* A *DP (Demat) account* includes all the shares that are present in an investor's Demat account after the clearing process is completed. There are three subcategories of holdings within a DP account:
## *Net Authorized Quantity*: The number of shares that are fully authorized and available for trading.
## *Open Authorized Quantity*: The number of shares that are authorized but not yet settled.
## *Pledged Quantity*: The number of shares that have been pledged as collateral for margin funding.
# *MTF (Margin Trading Facility) Account*: An *MTF account* contains holdings that were bought through margin trading. This account allows investors to buy securities by paying a fraction of the total value while the broker finances the remaining amount.
# *Haircut (Safety Margin Calculation)*: The *haircut* is not an account but a risk management related calculation using percentage defined. In Margin Trading Facility (MTF), a "haircut" is the percentage reduction applied to the market value of a security used as collateral, ensuring brokers have a risk buffer against potential price drops.

*Holdings management in the Trading System using Application or files:*

# Manual entries: *Manual Entry*: Traders or dealers can manually enter the values for different types of accounts.
Menu Path: ADMIN-CTCL/Surveillance/Holdings management/Manual entry

column1: system lag issue after RMS popup
column41:
critical system lag issue after the RMS popup focus behavior was modified on our dealer terminals.

 

*Background*

Previously, we experienced disruptions where RMS limit alerts would automatically shift system focus to the popup window, negatively impacting trade executions. To address this, we requested a change to prevent the popup from taking focus. 

 

*Current Issue*

While the focus change has been successfully implemented today, it has introduced a significant new problem:

* *Severe system lag* affecting all F&O trading systems during RMS popup reception
* The system continuously receives RMS popups in the background
* *System becomes unresponsive* for any operations while these popup messages are appearing
* Performance degradation confirmed by all F&O Dealers.
* *System resumes normal operation* only after the popup messages stop appearing
* Impact extends across all F&O operations during popup activity periods

 

*Key Point:* The lag occurs specifically while receiving continuous RMS popups - once the popup messages cease, the system returns to normal performance mode.



*Patch Details* 

*GETSManager_5.0.300924_Console_RH8_221225 + 241225 For Schema*

*GETSClient_5.0.300924_181225*

column1: Issue Description: GETS Dynamic Watch Arbitrage – Incorrect Exchange Feature Mapping Causing User Limit Exceed Error
column41:
Issue Description: GETS Dynamic Watch Arbitrage – Incorrect Exchange Feature Mapping Causing User Limit Exceed Error

* Licenses:

NSE FO: 1 license

BSE FO: 2 licenses

* Dealers:

Dealer 1: Mapped to both NSE and BSE exchanges

Dealer 2: Mapped only to BSE exchange

* Issue Explanation:

For Dealer 1, GETS Dynamic Watch Arbitrage product features are correctly mapped for both NSE FO and BSE FO.

For Dealer 2, only BSE exchange is mapped.

However, in the Product Feature Mapping, when only BSE FO features are selected for Dealer 2, the NSE FO feature options get selected automatically by default.

* Impact:

Because NSE FO features are auto-selected even though Dealer 2 is not mapped to NSE and the client has only 1 NSE FO license, the system counts extra usage.

Due to this incorrect feature mapping, Dealer 2 gets “User Limit Exceed” error while logging in to Algo.

* Expected Behavior:

When a dealer is mapped only to BSE exchange, only BSE FO product features should be selectable.

NSE FO features should not be auto-selected if the dealer is not mapped to NSE.

column1: API: Maintain order details in Redis and furnish cached entries for Order List and Order Status API
column41:
*Objective:*

To avoid querying the database for retrieving order list, order details and order status.



*Process:*

* Build a pipe between Iris and (?) to receive all order updates in real-time.
* Update the order details in Redis.
* Use Redis to serve all applicable requests to avoid load on DB and improve response time.
* Refresh Redis from DB upon startup, while ensuring there are no:
** Duplications (Scenario: Entry being present in DB as well as received from the pipe)
** Misses (Scenario: Entry absent in DB during fetch and missed it from the pipe as it was not established on time)



*Key Considerations:*

* Use Redis filters to get filtered results as necessary, E.g. For pending orders
* Flag based (Separate from other flags) so as to not impact other users.
* The component which maintains the Redis cache does not necessarily have to be Iris
** Iris will read the cache
* Should be robust and accurate enough to rely on Redis for getting order details in non API scenarios.
* A light weight access class can help drive adoption elsewhere. Seek data from this class only.

column41:
h3. Issue Description

The client was facing an *“ISIN Not Found” error* while uploading the file using *Shift + E*. Due to this error, the file upload process was failing.

h3. Our Observations and Analysis Steps Performed 

# *Initial File Validation*
#* Attempted file upload failed with _ISIN Not Found_ error.
# *Sheet-Level Changes*
#* In the upload file, under *Upload 2 Sheet*, the *Exchange* was changed from *NSE* to *BSE*.
#* Assumed that junk characters might be causing issues.
#* Identified and deleted *empty columns and empty rows* from the file.
# *Flag Configuration*
#* Updated the following flags:
#* BSECashUpload_InstTypeMISC = true
BSECashUpload_Deleted = true
BSECashUpload_Eligible = true
# Contract Handling
#* Downloaded *CM Improper Contract*.
#* Performed *Re-BOD*.
#* Uploaded *Normal Contract* again and performed *Re-BOD* once more.
# *Database Verification*
#* Checked the database and observed that *BSE contracts were not uploaded*.
# *CTCLManager.ini Configuration Check*
#* Found below flags set to {{false}}:

contractpath\BSEScriptcheck = false
contractpath\BSEScriptdetailscheck = false

* Changed both flags to {{true}}.
* Re-uploaded contracts and rechecked the database.
* Issue persisted — *BSE contracts were still not available* in the database.
* *Dashboard Verification*
** Checked *Contract Path* from the dashboard.
** Necessary contracts were showing as *ticked*.
** Observed that the *client does not have a BSE license enabled*.

----

The client *does not have a valid BSE license*.
Due to the absence of the BSE license:

* BSE contracts could not be uploaded.
* ISIN validation failed.
* File upload resulted in an *ISIN Not Found* error.

Informed the client that *BSE license is mandatory* for BSE contract upload and ISIN validation.

Advised the client to *apply for a BSE license*.

Once the BSE license is activated, the file upload issue should be resolved.

----

column1: Intelligent Test Plan from Commits
column41:
h2. *Purpose:*

{quote}_I want to integrate Kiwi TCMS (strong open-source choice) with JIRA. We have JIRA and GitHub integration so commits for a bug fix in JIRA are linked Every bug is linked to a test case (right now test case is just a JIRA type)._

 _I want to create an intelligence (based on past data) wherein, if a fix is done (or code change of any kind), based on the code lines affected by previous bug fixes, Can i create a list of impacted test cases which should be again tested? And create a sort of automatic test plan based on the latest commits? Or something alternative that works._ 

_I am looking at better coverage since we don't have formal impact analysis which can determine which test cases need to be tested apart from the obvious ones. I want to use possibly AI to detect it and create a test plan accordingly. Possible?_{quote}



h2. *Solution:*

Short answer: *yes, it’s possible*, and you can do this *incrementally* without boiling the ocean.
Long answer: what you’re describing is essentially *AI-assisted change impact analysis + risk-based test selection*, and it fits _very well_ with *JIRA + GitHub + Kiwi TCMS*.

Below is a *practical, architecture-level answer*, not marketing fluff.

----

h2. 1. First, a reality check (important)

What you want *cannot work reliably* unless you establish *explicit traceability* first.

AI can _enhance_ impact analysis, but it *cannot infer ground truth* if:

* Test cases aren’t linked to *code areas / components*
* Bugs don’t consistently reference *files, modules, or functions*
* Commits don’t reference *JIRA IDs*

The good news:
👉 You already have *JIRA ↔ GitHub* linkage
👉 You already link *bugs ↔ test cases*

So you’re *80% there*.

----

h2. 2. Target end state (what “good” looks like)

When a PR is merged:

# Detect *changed files / functions*
# Determine *historically associated bugs*
# Map those bugs to *test cases*
# Rank impacted test cases by *risk / probability*
# Automatically create a *Kiwi TCMS Test Plan*
# Push links back to *JIRA*

This is achievable.

----

h2. 3. Required data model (minimum viable)

You need to normalize the following signals:

h3. A. From GitHub

* Commit hash
* Files changed
* (Optional but powerful) Function/method names
* JIRA issue ID (already present)

h3. B. From JIRA

* Issue type (Bug / Story / Task)
* Component / Module
* Linked test cases (current model)

h3. C. From Kiwi TCMS

* Test Case ID
* Tags / Components
* Linked JIRA issue(s)
* Historical failures (very important)

----

h2. 4. How Kiwi TCMS fits in (very well, actually)

Kiwi TCMS has:

* REST APIs
* Test case tagging
* Test plan automation
* JIRA integration support

h3. Best practice

*Stop using JIRA issue type as “test case”* long-term.
Instead:

* Keep _requirements / bugs_ in JIRA
* Move *actual test cases* into Kiwi TCMS
* Maintain *bidirectional links*

This gives you clean separation and richer metadata.

----

h2. 5. Change impact analysis – practical approaches

h3. Level 1 (No AI, fast ROI – do this first)

*Rule-based impact selection*

# For each commit:
#* Extract changed files
# Map files → components/modules
# Select test cases where:
#* {{test_case.component == changed_component}}
#* OR {{test_case.tag matches file path}}
# Add all *regression tests* tagged for that component

✔ Works
✔ Deterministic
✔ Auditable
❌ Over-inclusive sometimes

This alone will improve coverage massively.

----

h3. Level 2 (Historical intelligence – highly effective)

Build a *Change → Bug → Test graph*

{noformat}File A changed
  ├─ Bug-123 (past)
  │    ├─ TC-45
  │    └─ TC-78
  └─ Bug-456
       └─ TC-12
{noformat}

Now:

* When {{File A}} changes again
* Re-select TC-45, TC-78, TC-12 automatically

This is *very powerful* and doesn’t even need ML initially.

*Data source*:

* Past Git commits
* JIRA bug links
* Kiwi TCMS test case links

----

h3. Level 3 (AI / ML based scoring – what you actually want)

Now AI makes sense.

h4. Features you can feed a model:

* Files changed (paths, tokens)
* Diff size
* Bug frequency per file
* Past test failure rates
* Time since last failure
* Developer / module ownership
* Test execution cost (optional)

h4. Model output:

* Probability that a test case will fail
* Ranked list of test cases

This becomes *Risk-Based Testing (RBT)*.

💡 Start with:

* Gradient Boosting / Random Forest
* Later, NLP embeddings on diffs if needed

----

h2. 6. Automatic test plan creation (Kiwi TCMS)

Workflow:

# GitHub webhook → your service
# Extract:
#* Commit(s)
#* JIRA IDs
#* Changed files
# Run impact logic (rule-based + ML)
# Select top N test cases
# Create Test Plan via Kiwi TCMS API
# Attach:
#* Git commit
#* JIRA issues
# Post comment in JIRA:
“Automated impact test plan created: TP-123”

This is *clean, auditable, and scalable*.

----

h2. 7. Where AI helps vs where it doesn’t

h3. AI is good at:

* Ranking relevance
* Detecting non-obvious relationships
* Reducing test scope intelligently

h3. AI is *bad* at:

* Replacing traceability
* Explaining decisions without structure
* Handling missing metadata

So:

{quote}*Structure first, AI second*{quote}

----

h2. 8. Tooling stack (practical)

* *Backend*: Python (FastAPI)
* *Data*: PostgreSQL
* *ML*: scikit-learn initially
* *Integration*:
** GitHub Webhooks
** JIRA REST API
** Kiwi TCMS REST API

No vendor lock-in.

----

h2. 9. Alternative / complementary ideas

h3. A. Test impact via coverage (if automated tests exist)

* Map test → code coverage
* Any touched line triggers that test
Very accurate, but needs instrumentation.

h3. B. Hybrid model (recommended)

* Coverage for automated tests
* Historical + AI for manual tests

As a result, when a new connection was established, incoming data was appended to the existing buffer, leading to the formation of corrupted or invalid packets.

This issue has been addressed by implementing a mechanism to ensure that all residual data associated with the previous connection is cleared prior to establishing a new session. This prevents unintended data carryover and ensures the integrity of packet processing.

column1: Refactoring activity for GNexLayer (Proposal for approval)
column41:
Our current implementation is functionally correct but requires structural improvements and code refactoring. The objective is to introduce a shared Go workspace–based utility module and standardize common functionality across all services without using a sidecar pattern.
This refactor will not change any core business logic; it will only improve the architecture, maintainability, and consistency.

*Scope of Work*

h3. *1. Repository Synchronization*

* Sync *develop* and *main* branches (they have diverged).
* Resolve merge conflicts and ensure both branches are aligned before refactor.

----

h3. *2. Introduce Common Utility Service (Go Workspace)*

A new shared utility workspace will provide:

h4. *Core Implementations*

* Centralized *Zap logger* configuration.
* Common *request validator*.
* Shared *database connectivity* layer.

h4. *Helper Utilities*

* *Redis* helper.
* *Consul* helper.
* *Vault* helper.
* *DB helper* (shared query utilities).
* *ClickHouse* helper.
* *Prometheus* metrics implementation.

----

h3. *3. System-Wide Improvements*

* Remove *all hardcoded variables* → move to configs/env/Consul/Vault.
* Implement *centralized error handling*.
* Standardize *error response structure* across all services.
* Create *common middleware*:
** Authentication middleware
** Request validation middleware
* Introduce *centralized Base64 decoding* utility.

----

h2. *Non-Functional Impact*

* *Core business logic will remain unchanged.*
* Only architectural and implementation-level changes.
* Requires *sanity testing* across all services after refactoring.

----

h2. *Timeline*

* Estimated time: *1 week (5 working days)* for complete refactoring and integration



*For any suggestion please feel free to comment out here*

Change the logic of create lToken of DIDX,DFUT scrip for NSE and BSE
column41:
*NSE*

For NSE DIDX lToken is created Following Sequence

BANKNIFTY = 1

NIFTY = 2

FINNIFTY = 3

MIDCPNIFTY = 4



For Derive Future lToken is created using Following Logic:

(DIDXToken * 100) + Week of Year.

For Example: Nifty(Expiry: 6JAN26)  =

DIDX Token of Nifty is 2.  and 6JAN is 2nd Week Of Year.

Hence Nifty6JAN DFUT lToken is (2*100)+2 = 202.



*BSE*

For BSE  DIDX lToken is created Following Sequence

SENSEX = 1

BANKEX = 2

(This lDIDX ltoken is also written in Derive_Future.txt File which is present in Release path)



For Derive Future lToken is created Logic is same as NSE

(DIDXToken * 100) + Week of Year.

For Example: SENSEX(Expiry: 11 DEC 2025)  =

DIDX Token of SENSEX is 1.  and 11 DEC is 50th Week Of Year.

Hence SENSEX 11 DEC DFUT lToken is (1*100)+50 = 150.



*Note:*  This logic is for Unique token for all server. solved Issue of Different ltoken created for different server.

column1: Python Script: Pull commits and highlight ones without a JIRA ID
column41:
{quote}_“Create and run a CRON job to track commits in GIT without a mention of a Jira ID. “_{quote}



Create a python script which will accept the following parameters:

* gitlab path
* app id 
* repo/branch
* period (in days)
* email id list (string with comma separated ids)



It will pull the data based on the parameters,

* iterate entries and look for the regular expression, viz: *GETSCTCL-\d+*
* create a list of commits that do not contain the pattern, and prepare a report with:
** Commit Owner
** Date/Time
** Revision number
** Commit string
* Attach the report in an email and send to the intended recipients (accepted as parameter)



The report should omit the entries found for merging like:

* Merge branch 'console_rhl8' into 'PROD_120925'
* Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/console_rhl8' into Pravin_console_rhl8
* Skipping entries like “Merge branch” and “Merge remote-tracking branch” should help filter out the entries
** To make this more usable, create a separate array of keywords (patterns) to skip
** And iterate that to filter out the necessary entries
** We can then add to this pattern array (rather than deep in the code) to keep this script more accurate over time



Once the script is ready, it will be added to a cron job somewhere in the Greeksoft network by the IT team.

*Observation 1 :*

# *After re-login, when the download process begins*, 7-digit order numbers are generated for newly placed orders.
# During the download process, an order was received that originated from the NEAT application (another vendor).
This is observed in the log file 2025Dec19NSEInteractive_2.log, where an FO orderEntryResponse with GreekCode = 5516 shows lOurOrderNo = 1020000.
*This order originated from the NEAT application and had Our Order No = 0.*
# Since this order was not placed through our system, lOurOrderNo was not available. Therefore, lOurOrderNo = 1020000 was assigned to this order, and the *record was inserted into the OrderInfo table*.
# Once the download process is completed, *ClientCommunicator retrieves the maximum lOurOrderNo from the OrderInfo table and uses it as the starting point for subsequent orders*.
# *Consequently, all manual orders placed after re-login/downloading are assigned sequential lOurOrderNo values, starting from 1020001, 1020002, 1020003, and onwards.*

*Observation 2 :*


*Based on further analysis, it appears that either an incorrect packet was received from the exchange .* As a result, invalid data for lOurOrderNo = 1020000 was recorded in the OrderInfo database.
This is reflected in the logs, where the order is shown as originating from the NEAT application and having Our Order No = 0.

column1: Server side logging for order cancellation.
column41:
Implementation details:

Added “EnableCancelOrdLog“ to enable server side logging for cancel order. It is auto generated flag and default value is false.

To enable this functionality need to set it as true in INI. On ClientCommunicator startup this flag will create.

If we enabled this functionality and cancelled orders then it will log in “YYMMMDDCancelOrderLog.log“ file.

Following greek codes are handled for logging,

#define GIC_ORD_OFFLINE_CANCEL_REQ                      5529
#define GIC_ORDER_CANCEL_REQ                            5508
#define GIC_KILL_SWITCH_REQ                             6507
#define	GIC_SPREAD_ORD_CANCEL_REQ                       5706
#define GIC_OFFLINE_2LEG_ORDER_CANCEL_REQ                3360

column41:
1 Set dealer count = 100, group count = 5, and user count = 1000 in the CTCLManager.ini file.

2 Perform BOD and create a new retailer, e.g., RET1.

3 In the indextoclient table, system set the igreekuserorinvestorid for RET1 to 106.

4 Perform EOD.

5 Now change the dealer count in CTCLManager.ini from 100 to 200.

6 Start the CTCLManager component again.
7 On the console, a message appears asking whether you want to reset the user count. Press "Yes".

8 After the Manager component starts successfully:

           >In the indextoclient table, the igreekuserorinvestorid for RET1 still shows 106 instead of 206.

           >In the CTCLManager.ini file, the user count is automatically updated from 1000 to 1205, which is incorrect.

9 Create a new dealer, e.g., DEAL1.
10 In the indextoclient table, DEAL1 gets assigned igreekuserorinvestorid = 107 instead of 2.

Note:
The same issue occurs with group count.

Observation

The issue does not occur when starting the Manager using the “CTCLManager_ui” command.

Impact

REL_3009_CONSOL & REL_2512_CONSOL: RMS crashes if the dealer count exceeds the dealer count configured in the ini file.

RMS crash is handled in REL_1209 by preventing creation of dealers beyond the configured dealer count in the ini file.

column1: Require VVAP-Based Execution in GEA strategy
column41:
+Require VVAP-Based Execution in GEA strategy+



*(Volume Weighted Average Price Variation)*–based execution within the client's execution algo module.
The client has requested *two variants* of VVAP calculation:

# *Static VWAP*
# *Dynamic VWAP*

Both approaches rely on *ATP (Average Traded Price)* captured at a specific time, and a *percentage input (MPP%)* entered by the client.

!VVAP_SS.png|width=671,alt="VVAP_SS.png"!



+*Affected Field: MPP% (Attached Screen Shot for reference).*+

+*Affected Segment= EQ and FO.*+

----

# *Static VWAP*

In Static VWAP, system captures ATP at *09:08:00* and *does not update it during the trading day*.

h3. *Business Rules*

# ATP at 09:08:00 becomes the reference ATP for entire session.
# Once user provides MPP%, system computes:
#* *Upper Price Band = ATP + (ATP × MPP%)*
#* *Lower Price Band = ATP – (ATP × MPP%)*
# These prices remain *unchanged* throughout the trading session.
# Algo validates each outgoing order:
#* If price > MAX → order blocked
#* If price < MIN → order blocked

h3. *Use Case Example*

Buy Side

* ATP at 09:08 → *₹105*
* MPP% → *2%*
* MAX = 105 + 2.1 = *107.10*
* MIN = 105 – 2.1 = *102.90*

Sell Side

* ATP at 09:08 → *₹105*
* MPP% → *2%*
* MAX = 105 - 2.1 = *102.90*
* MIN = 105 + 2.1 = *107.10*

----

# *Dynamic VWAP*
In Dynamic VWAP, ATP is rechecked periodically based on *client-defined interval* (e.g., every 5 sec, 30 sec, 1 min).


h3. *Business Rules*

# ATP snapshot at 09:08:00 is initial ATP.
# System takes *new ATP values* at specified intervals.
# Every time ATP changes, system recalculates *VVAP band*:
#* MAX = newATP + (newATP × MPP%)
#* MIN = newATP – (newATP × MPP%)
# Algo adjusts its order execution band dynamically.

All passwords must be stored in the database using secure hashing algorithms. Plaintext or reversible encryption methods are strictly prohibited.

* Use [Argon2id|https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html#argon2id] with a minimum configuration of 19 MiB of memory, an iteration count of 2, and 1 degree of parallelism.

column495: 21/Jan/26 5:27 PM;712020:2bf45437-71cc-46f5-acad-f438d576a61b;This is not an issue. When the order is generated, the exchange is in the pre-open session while our system is in the market open session. As a result, our system sends the order in the normal manner, but the exchange treats it as a new order and holds it in the pre-open session. During the pre-open session, the exchange does not send any cancellation or trade responses, which is why the order remains pending on our side in the F3 window. Once the exchange moves to the open market session, it sends either a cancellation or a trade confirmation for those orders.

column1: GNexLayer: HarmoniaCraft for data sync between GNexLayer and GETS Manager
column41:
Typical flow in case of Funds and Margin sync up flow diagram and explanation are given below:



!image-20260202-064047.png|width=1441,alt="image-20260202-064047.png"!



*HarmoniaCraft*: Role of this service is to route incoming packet from backend GETSManager(OMS) to correct microservice based on Message code by placing the packet on respective subject, and also pass any updates/changes from GNexLayer to GETSManager.

*PaymentCraft*: This service handles all Funds, Margin and Banks related packet and updates in respective data store(s) like database tables and/or Redis.

Validation is required for specific fields while calling the ProductConversionAPI
column41:
Issues observed while calling ProductConversionAPI:

1.Validation required for Traded Quantity
The API currently accepts values greater than the actual traded quantity. It should restrict input to the valid traded quantity only.

2.Validation required for Total Quantity
The API is allowing quantities exceeding the total available quantity. Proper validation must be implemented to prevent this.

3.Response Validation for Invalid Inputs
When invalid data is passed, the API response does not display a specific error message related to the incorrect field. The response should clearly indicate the error corresponding to the invalid input field.

4.Validation required for gscid field
The system should not allow product conversion if the gscid field is missing or blank. Proper validation must be implemented to handle this scenario.

5.Validation required for product tpye field.
The system should not allow product conversion if the product tpye field is  blank or Invalid

6.Validation required for iGiveUpStatus field.
The system should not allow product conversion if the iGiveUpStatus field is blank or Invalid.

7. Validation required for the Quantity field based on Lot Size for F&O tokens.
The system should not allow product conversion if the quantity does not match the valid lot size for the respective F&O contract.

column1: Watchlist screen scrolling not working when more data is present in MCG app
column41:
*Description:*
When the screen contains a large amount of data, the scroll behavior does not work correctly. The app bar (MCG client) does not show/hide as expected during scrolling. Instead of smoothly hiding on scroll-down and showing on scroll-up, it behaves inconsistently or gets stuck.

*Proposed Solution* 
:-
Previously, the Watchlist screen used the common *SFGrid* package, which caused scroll issues and improper App Bar show/hide behavior when large data sets were loaded.
To resolve this, we will *remove dependency on the common SFGrid package* for the Watchlist screen and instead *implement all required functionality individually using a ListView*.



Implement all watchlist-related features manually, including:

* New UI components
* Broadcast logic
* Delete watchlist
* Rename watchlist
* Add new symbols
* Any additional watchlist interactions/features from the old SFGrid implementation

In your case, when a user logs in for the first time, then logs out and logs in again, the system accepts biometric authentication. However, in our case, we do not show the biometric option after logout. As per your observation, this is considered an issue, but for us it is not an issue.

Our functionality works as follows: when a user logs in for the first time, they are required to enter the MPIN. If the user does not log out and simply swipes the app away, they will continue to get the biometric option on reopening the app. But if the user logs out and then logs in again, they must re-enter the MPIN. This is because a different user might log in, and for security reasons, we require MPIN authentication after every logout.

Required in house setting as per exchange IDs
column41:
At present we have flags fir in house setting for all exchanges and all segments. We want that the ini setting should be applicable only to those IDs that are mentioned/included in the ini file below the given flag. 

For rest of the IDs the flag mentioned should not be applicable.

User can add multiple IDs by adding commas in flag



For eg: 

we have 4 NSE Equity ids as (44385, 47718,47719,47930)

The flag InHouseSettings\NSEEquityInHouse=true should work only for 44385,47718 .

For rest all IDs (47719,47930) the flag should not be applicable, i.e., it should work as normal (No in house).

Accordingly user can achieve with inhouse & without inhouse functionality .

*InHouseSettings\NSEEquityInHouse=true*
*NSEEquityUserIds=44385, 47718*

similarly for all exchange & all segments these flags should be created 

InHouseSettings\BINXInHouse=false
InHouseSettings\BSECurrencyInHouse=false
InHouseSettings\BSEInHouse=false
InHouseSettings\MCX_StrategyId=11111
InHouseSettings\NINXInHouse=false
InHouseSettings\NSECommodityInHouse=false
InHouseSettings\NSECurrencyInHouse=false
*InHouseSettings\NSEEquityInHouse=true*
*NSEEquityUserIds=44385, 47718*
InHouseSettings\NSEFutureInHouse=false
InHouseSettings\NSEOFSInHouse=false
InHouseSettings\NSESLBMInHouse=false





Needed for all exchange and all segments.

Need to give a new below user management having columns: Exchange, segment, UserID (selected by default), type (dropdown for “vendor”, ”inhouse”).





Implementation Details:

Added following 2 flags in INI to enable this functionality,

*EnableInHouseSettings* = To enable/disable InHouse functionality. Default value is false. Autogenerated flag on CC startup.

*InHouseDetails*= Need to set string for inhouse. Default value is empty string. Autogenerated flag on CC startup.

All old Inhouse related flags are not in use now have to use only above 2 flags.

String format “EXCHSEG-TraderId-AlgoId”

Following is the example for the same,

NEQ-44384-12565|NFO-38712-22334|

Note: Append | after last field as mentioned above.

Need to mentioned following format for EXCHSEG field,

NEQ

NFO

NCD

NCOM

NINX

BEQ

BFO

BCD

BCOM

BINX.

In case of setting is set for specific traderid then in algo orders INI mentioned algoId  should go in algo orders. In this case, AlgoId set on ADMIN should not go in algo orders .

After setting flags component restart is required.

column41:
DP holding need to allow for square off from dealer and admin from holding position square off function 



*Observations from the Testing Team*

* Validation is required when squaring off DP from the *Alt+F9* window.
* Square-off should be allowed only for the *authorized quantity* of the particular symbol. It should allow square-off only up to the authorized quantity.
* Square-off should be allowed *only if the holding quantity for the particular symbol is pledged*.
* If the *_Pledge Block_* option is enabled in the *RMS General Settings* window, then square-off should *not* be allowed if the holding quantity is pledged.
* If the holding quantity for a particular symbol is *neither pledged nor authorized*, square-off should *not* be allowed.
* In the case of *buyback*, the validation sequence should match the manual *F1/F2* sequence.

A provision needs to be implemented in system to calculate margins for NCDEX option contracts using *BMS_RA00.xml*.

When we modify an IOB rule that is already added in Ctrl+G and has different traded and placed quantities, the following behavior occurs:

As per Ctrl+G functionality, it places equal quantities for both buy and sell orders. After these orders are traded, the rule is removed from Ctrl+G.

column1: Capture and Store Client IP Address During API Order Placement
column41:
Requirement:
A new field should be added to the API order request to accept the client’s IP address as input.

* This field is not required to be included in the API response.
* The provided IP address should be stored in the database and/or application logs for audit and tracking purposes.

Purpose:
Capturing and storing the client IP address will enable future audit inspections and improve traceability of API-based order placements.



{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
Prasad’s View


The IP should not be put in API order request as it does not guarantee authenticity, and essentially requires trust.

The IP should be _captured_ on server end based on the client IP detected by the TCP/IP protocol for the REST API request. This value then needs to be either logged in an audit trail file (like how web servers do) or store in the DB in a separate mapping table that could look like this:

* lourorderno
* gscid
* API + parameters
* ip_address
* timestamp
{panel}

column1: API Should Return Appropriate Error Response When Order Is Not Successfully Placed
column41:
When a client places an order through the API, in some cases the order is not actually placed — even though there is no IRIS rejection or RMS rejection. Despite this, the API still returns a 200 OK success response without any error message or error code, and a *gorderid* is generated.

This behavior makes it difficult for clients to determine the actual order status, as fetching the order status using the orderId status returns a *null* response.

The client requests that, in such cases where the order is not successfully placed, the API response should clearly indicate the failure and include an appropriate error message or error code instead of returning a generic success response.



Requirement by MOSL-HVT Project

column1: TTFIX | Handling for Strike Price [for symbols like: OG, OG1, OG2, OG3, OG4, OG5]
column41:
Ideally, we expect that TT should send the strike price for {{OG}} symbols in the same format as it does for other symbols. Specifically, the strike price should be sent in full (e.g., 464000 for {{OG}}) so that when the calculation is performed (i.e., multiplying by the display factor of 0.01), the result is as expected (4640.00). This would ensure there are no issues with market data requests or placing orders, without needing to add a separate ruleset for {{OG}} symbols.

It seems there might be an issue with how the strike price or display factor is being transmitted for {{OG}} symbols. If the strike price were provided in the same manner as it is for other symbols (e.g., 3700000 for NQ), the system should work without any problems and eliminate the need for applying special rules.

 

Also,  *Last Traded Price (LTP)* of the asset token (e.g., *FUT script*) should serve as the strike price for the corresponding *OPT script*, or the *strike price of the OPT script* should be *within the range* of the *LTP of its FUT script*.

However, in our scenario, *when no ruleset is applied*, this relationship does not hold as expected.

*For example:* For GC, if the LTP is 39450, the strike price of the OPT script should be in the same range (e.g., or near 39450).

column504: GNexLayer and GETS Manager integration for Trading using Mobile and Web applications

column1: Synchronizing IBT Users data between GETS Manager and GNexLayer
column41:
*Requirement*: GNexLayer is the middleware between end users and backend OMS (Connecting to exchanges). All user management typically happens in backend OMS. These user data (creation/updates) should be posted to GNexLayer as GNexLayer doesn't have user related data of its own. GNexLayer stores all user related data for its usage in its OWN data model designed for easy/fast access during processing.

      Any changes happening to user data in GNexLayer should be posted to backend main system like GETS Manager, and any changes to user data in GETS manager should be immediately posted to GNexLayer.

      User related data required for trading in the systems should be in synchronized all the time between GNexLayer and GETS Manager.

 

Following are the categories of data which should be in sync:

# Authentication: Login Id, password, previous passwords, MPIN, previouse Pins, user lock/unlock status.
# User profile data: Theme settings, Column profile, holdingFilter etc.
# Markets allowed for trading.
# Products allowed for trading.
# Brokerage template and charges.
# RMS expense master.
# Product master: One time setup, later changes as per requirement.
# Holdings
# Funds

column1: Devolvement margin need to calculate for MCX exchange
column41:
Devolvement refers to the conversion of an option contract into a futures contract of the same underlying. When commodity options are In the Money (ITM), they are devolved into the underlying futures contract. The strike price of the devolved options contract is the buy average for take delivery or the sell average for give delivery of the futures contract. If the option is ITM and there aren't sufficient margins in the Zerodha account to hold till expiry, then the position will be squared off after 7 PM on the expiry day. If there are sufficient margins in the trading account and an ITM option contract is held, it will be devolved into the underlying futures contract from the very next day of expiry.

On the options contract expiry date, all open ITM options contracts will be devolved into futures. The exchange blocks a margin equivalent to 25% of the futures margin required to hold the ITM option contract 2 days before expiry and 50% of the futures margin 1 day before expiry, and 100% of the futures margin for devolvement. Failing to produce the margin in the trading account can result in a square-off of open positions at Zerodha’s discretion. If the ITM options trade cannot be matched with a counterparty, it will be cash-settled.
Example Scenario

    Gold is at 31500 levels.
    GOLD 19JAN 31000 CE is an ITM option contract.
    On expiry day, GOLD 19JAN 31000 CE will devolve into GOLD 19FEB FUT, with a buy average of 31000.

Short position settlement happens based on the counter buyer consent. If a client has open hedge positions on expiry day, it may result in a net-off. In such an event, these positions won’t be carried forward. If Long futures and short call option positions are held, the short call option will be devolved into a short future position after 11:30 pm on the expiry day. In such a case, the positions will be netted off, and these won’t be carried forward.

column1: Save Holdings Locally in Mobile App.
column41:
*Issue Description:*
In conditions of low network bandwidth, live clients are currently unable to view their holdings due to delayed or failed data retrieval from the server.

*Proposed Solution:*
To address this, we plan to implement local storage of holdings data on the client’s device. The app will save the holdings data locally after the initial successful fetch. Subsequent updates to the holdings will only occur when user activities or other processes affect the holdings, thereby minimizing network dependency.

*Benefit:*
This approach ensures that clients with low network bandwidth can still access their holdings without interruption, providing a seamless user experience even in poor connectivity environments.

Holding upload files (DP Holdings, MTF Holdings, Other Formats) from the back office contain *extra blank spaces* in columns like *Symbol* and *Series*.

Because of this, the system shows an error:
*“Symbol and Series wrong”*, and the file fails to upload.



h3. *Temporary Fix:*

Manually removing the blank spaces from these columns allows the file to upload successfully.



System should *automatically trim* any *leading or trailing spaces* from key fields (like Symbol and Series) during file upload.

The order should allow modification and partial execution consistently, without rejection, until fully executed or cancelled.

column1: Expiry Date Mismatch in VB Greek: Thursday vs Tuesday Expiry
column41:
In VB Greek, the system automatically switches to the next month's data the day after the monthly expiry. This is currently set up for Thursday expiry. So, if the expiry is on a Thursday, the next day (Friday) the system shows the following month's information.

For example: If the expiry is on Thursday, September 25, 2025, then on Friday, September 26, 2025, when I log into VB Greek, it automatically shows the next month.

However, now the expiry day is Tuesday, but the system is still working based on Thursday expiry.

For example, the current expiry is Tuesday, September 30, but VB Greek started showing the next month from September 26, which is based on Thursday expiry.

Requirement to update the system to work according to the Tuesday expiry instead.

column1: BSE Derivatives - Increase in Number of Partitions from 12 to 14 in Equity Derivatives Segment
column41:
Trading Members are hereby informed that the number of partitions in the Equity Derivatives segment will be increased from 12 to 14, effective *October 13, 2025*. Each partition serves a set of products, and from the effective date, trading will be conducted across 14 partitions for all products. 

*Partition Information:*
Partition details are available in the Equity Derivatives master file (EQD_CODDMMYY.csv) under column 13 (Partition ID).

----

*Impact on ETI-Based Applications*

* All ETI applications utilizing Partition ID for retransmission of orders, trades, or other partition-oriented messages must be updated to query for 14 partitions instead of 12.
* The number of partitions is also included in the Session Logon Response (Template ID 10001) message of the ETI API under the field name NoOfPartition(1770).

----

*Product Movement*

* The Exchange will gradually create new products and may move certain products from the existing 12 partitions to new partitions 13 and 14.
* Any change in partition assignment will be reflected in the EQD_CODDMMYY.csv file.

----

*Impact on EMDI/EOBI*

* Movement of products between partitions will affect the existing EOBI/EOBI streams, as these are partition-wise multicast streams.
* Market data for a product will be available only from the multicast stream of the partition to which it has been moved.
* Please refer to the BOLTPLUS Configuration file version 1.15 (attached) for details on partition-wise multicast streams of EMDI and EOBI. The file is also available at [http://www.bseindia.com/nta.aspx|http://www.bseindia.com/nta.aspx|smart-link] .

All members are requested to make necessary changes in their EOBI/EMDI applications to accommodate ongoing product movements.

----

*Testing and Simulation*

* A mock session will be conducted on *October 10, 2025*, for members to test the addition of new partitions.
* Partitions 13 and 14 will be available in the Simulation environment for testing from *October 4, 2025*.[^Annexure (224b694f-43aa-4361-b40f-eaaadd8c4a62).zip] [^20250926-66 (0e129aff-c714-4456-a7dc-c9288e751aae).pdf]

column1: Requirement for New Endpoint to Fetch Broadcast Data
column41:
*Requirement:*

A new API endpoint is required to provide broadcast data for subscribed tokens. For example, if a client subscribes to 10 tokens, the system should return the broadcast data for _all_ 10 tokens at fixed intervals (e.g., every 10 milliseconds), regardless of whether there has been a price tick or update for each individual token. The response must consistently include data for all subscribed tokens in each interval.

column1: High-Performance GET Endpoint for Real-Time Net Position Retrieval
column41:
*Requirement:*
Develop a new GET API endpoint that delivers faster response times compared to the existing endpoint:
{{http://restapi.greeksoft.in:3333/getStrategyNameWiseNetPositionDetail?gscid=NTD&type=expiry}}

As per Ajit Sir’s suggestion, we will reduce the number of table dependencies involved in generating the response, in order to improve performance.

The client expects to retrieve the NET Position data instantly, i.e., at the same moment the position is created.

column1: Revision in tick size of Stock Options in F&O Segment
column41:
Revision in tick size of Stock Options in F&O Segment This is in reference to circulars NSE/FAOP/62175 dated May 24, 2024 and NSE/FAOP/67134 dated March 13, 2025, where Exchange had informed about revision in tick size for Stock Futures contracts.

Members are requested to note that the revision in tick size shall now be applicable to Stock Options contracts also as below:

|Underlying Security Price|Current Tick Size|Proposed Tick Size|
|Below 250|0.05|0.01|
|≥ 250 |0.05|0.05 (unchanged)|

The above will be effective from the trade date of November 03, 2025. The first revision of tick size as per the proposed tick size for stock options contracts shall be undertaken on October 31, 2025 (EOD) based on closing price on the last trading day in CM Segment on October 31, 2025.

column1: Changes in VittOrderAdapter and VittGMBSAdapter with respect to Server side Changes.
column55:
* I worked on improving the *VittOrderAdapter* by adding more detailed and expressive logs. The goal was to make sure that whenever an order is placed, we can clearly see its entire journey in the system — from the time it is created, passed through the adapter, and finally until the response comes back. This will make it much easier for us to track and understand what is happening with each order.
* I broke down the process into multiple *checkpoints* and added logs at each of those steps. For example, we now log when the order request is first received, when the adapter processes it, when it is sent forward, and finally when the exchange responds. This step-by-step tracking helps in identifying exactly where a problem may occur if something goes wrong.
* I also made sure the log messages include all the *important details* like the order ID, the symbol, the exchange name, the quantity, and the price. Having this information in the logs makes it very easy to pick out a specific order and follow its progress. Earlier logs were not giving us such a complete picture, but now we can see everything at a glance.;19/Sep/25 4:10 PM;036f177f-fdb2-413b-be85-28d0cdd5d869;18000
column56:
* After writing the logs, I ran *tests with sample orders* to make sure everything is working properly. I checked that all log entries were appearing in the right order and that no steps were skipped. This gave me confidence that the logging system is reliable and will work the same way in production.
* I coordinated with *@saunish sheth* to review the order execution from the exchange side. We matched the actual trades being executed with the logs we generated in the system. This helped to confirm that the logs are accurate and reflect the true status of the order.
* I also took some time to *compare the old logging system with the new one*. The old logs were very minimal and sometimes confusing. The new logs are much more detailed and easier to read, which will save us time whenever we need to debug issues or check how an order was processed.;19/Sep/25 4:12 PM;036f177f-fdb2-413b-be85-28d0cdd5d869;16200
column57:
* Worked on the *VittGMBSAdapter* where issues were reported in the *Broadcast structure*, specifically related to scanner metrics. This issue was first highlighted by *@saunish sheth*, and I started debugging the component to understand what was going wrong.
* While debugging, I carefully reviewed how the broadcast data was being structured and shared across the system. I identified that the existing structure was not correctly handling some of the values that are critical for scanner metrics, which was leading to inconsistencies.
* I coordinated with *@Hitesh patil* to verify the expected behavior and cross-check the scanner metrics issue. With his input and further debugging, I made the required *structural changes* in the broadcast logic to ensure the data is now being sent in the proper format.;19/Sep/25 4:16 PM;036f177f-fdb2-413b-be85-28d0cdd5d869;18000
column58:
* In parallel, I also worked on resolving another issue related to *BcastCraft*, which was earlier pointed out by *@mukesh kashyap*. The BcastCraft issue was tied to the way broadcasts were being handled internally, and it required adjustments similar to the ones made for the broadcast structure.
* Debugged the BcastCraft flow and applied targeted fixes to resolve the error conditions that were reported. Post-fix testing showed that the broadcasts were now functioning properly without errors or dropped updates.
* Both issues (scanner metrics and BcastCraft) were validated after the changes, and I confirmed with the respective team members that the problems were resolved to their satisfaction.;19/Sep/25 4:17 PM;036f177f-fdb2-413b-be85-28d0cdd5d869;14400
column59:
* Implemented a new feature where *LogTime* is added in *Redis* whenever an Order Response or Trade Response packet is received. This ensures that the system always keeps track of the exact time the last packet was received.
* By storing the *last packet received timestamp* in Redis, we now have a reliable way to reference it in the future, which will be especially useful during debugging, monitoring, and recovery scenarios. This helps in analyzing whether there were any delays or missing packets in the order/trade flow.
* Validated this change by placing multiple orders and trades, then cross-checking Redis entries to confirm that the timestamps were updating correctly with each new packet. This confirmed that the functionality is working as expected.;19/Sep/25 4:22 PM;036f177f-fdb2-413b-be85-28d0cdd5d869;14400
column60:
* Had discussions with *@saunish sheth* about managing *broker-wise separated files on MinIO*, which plays an important role in the BOD (Beginning of Day) process. We reviewed how this separation could simplify file handling and improve operational clarity.
* Provided support in planning and helping with the broker-wise file handling process, ensuring that the system can easily distinguish and process files based on brokers during BOD activities.
* Later, while working on related flows, an *issue was found in Order Response handling*. This caused unexpected behavior during execution, so I started debugging to find the root cause.

column1: SEBI Lama Framework
column41:
SEBI LAMA  framework

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has introduced the

*LAMA (Logging and Monitoring Mechanism)* framework to address technical glitches in stockbrokers' electronic trading systems. This framework, outlined in a SEBI circular dated November 25, 2022, aims to protect investor interests and enable regulators to monitor stockbrokers' critical systems more effectively. 

----

How LAMA Works

* LAMA is an API-based system developed by stock exchanges to monitor and analyze the activities of specified stockbrokers' critical applications and infrastructure.
* It operates by collecting key performance metrics from stockbrokers' trading platforms every *five minutes* and sending them to the exchange via the LAMA API gateway.
* This mechanism allows for proactive monitoring of technical glitches, such as malfunctions in hardware, software, networks, processes, or electronic services.
* Alerts and reports are generated based on predefined parameters and thresholds, providing real-time insights into the trading platform's performance. 

Reporting Requirements

* Stockbrokers must report a technical glitch to the stock exchange within *one hour* of its occurrence.
* A Preliminary Incident Report needs to be submitted within *T+1 day* (the next business day).
* A Root Cause Analysis (RCA) report must be submitted within *14 days* of the incident. 

Additional Guidelines for Stockbrokers

* Stockbrokers are required to conduct capacity planning, ensuring their installed capacity is at least *1.5 times* the observed peak load during a calendar quarter.
* They must implement robust software updates, testing, and change management processes.
* Business Continuity Planning (BCP) and Disaster Recovery (DR) setups are mandated for specified stockbrokers.
* Compliance with DR site requirements and conducting live DR drills are also required. 

Benefits of LAMA

* Enhanced compliance with regulatory requirements.
* Improved performance optimization of trading systems.
* Increased data transparency for monitoring purposes.
* Facilitates real-time monitoring and alerting for potential issues.
* Aids in identifying and preventing glitches, improving system uptime and performance.
* Strengthens cybersecurity by monitoring for suspicious activity and potential threats. 

Impact on Brokers

* Brokers are required to connect to a single LAMA platform (currently hosted by NSE).
* Implementation may require investments in monitoring tools and robust infrastructure, potentially posing challenges for smaller firms.
* HDFC Securities was penalized for non-compliance with LAMA system implementation and other related norms.

column1: Log Analytics and Monitoring Application (LAMA)

{quote}SEBI had issued a circular for LAMA - Nov 25, 2022

Circular No.: SEBI/HO/MIRSD/TPD-1/P/CIR/2022/160.



Attached herewith an additional document from NSE related to LAMA.



_6.Monitoringmechanism:_

 

_6.1 Proactively and independently monitoring technical glitches shall be one of the approaches in mitigating the impact of such glitches.  In this context, the stock exchange shall build API based Logging and Monitoring Mechanism (LAMA)  to  be operated between stock exchanges and specified stockbrokers’ trading systems.  Under this mechanism, specified stockbrokers shall monitor key systems & functional parameters to ensure that their trading systems function in a smooth manner.  Stock exchanges shall, through the API gateway,  independently  monitor these key parameters to gauge the health of the trading systems of the specified stockbrokers._

 

 

_6.2 Stock Exchanges shall identify the key parameters in consultation with stockbrokers. These key parameters shall be monitored by specified stockbrokers and by stock exchanges, on a real time or on a near real time basis._

 

_6.3 Stock exchanges shall maintain a dedicated cell for monitoring the key parameters and the technical glitches occurring in stockbrokers’ trading systems.  The cell also shall intimate the specified stockbroker concerned immediately about the breach of the key parameters monitored under LAMA._

 

_6.4 Stock brokers and stock exchanges shall preserve the logs of the key parameters for a period of 30 days in normal course. However, if technical glitch takes place,  the  data related to the glitch, shall be maintained for a period of 2 years._{quote}

Gap fill for missed messages between GNexLayer and GETS Manager
column41:
Background, Current logic and its limitations and proposed approach

h2. Gap fill process between GNexLayer and backend GETS Manager

Gap fill is the process where a system requests missed messages (responses) from main or backend system with which its communicating for transactions. In our case messages are exchange orders/trades. During the gap fill process flow the GNexLayer will go in recovery mode and will reject orders till it completes the recovery process and then in availability or online mode. After completing recovery mode GNexLayer will go in online mode and will start accepting orders and function as usual.

Typically GNexLayer will be connected to brokers OMS (Order Management Systems) like GETS Manager via an adapter(specific to an OMS) component , and this backend OMS system will be connected to one or many exchanges (NSE, BSE etc. segment wise). Typically a sequence number like “Last activity reference number” with precision in nano seconds provided by exchanges can be maintained across various segments, and this number can be used as reference for downloading missed messages taking it as reference number or point.

There are two main reasons for Gap fill flow/process to get executed/initiated.

# Backend OMS or Broker system disconnects from exchange(s) because of some reason, so OMS system tries and fetches all missed messages/responses from exchange(s) during the disconnected period. After completing message  download and once in sync OMS sends message/trigger to Adapter component of GNexLayer. GNexLayer's adapter component notifies all dependent components that it is going into recovery mode and (waits for acknowledgement from dependent  process)*(Need discussion). Dependent services like OrderCraft on receiving recovery mode message from Adapter, Updates internal flag/variable for checking and stops accepting orders from connected clients.
# Adapter process connecting to ClientCommunicator (backend OMS) disconnects, or restarts or ClientCommunicator restarts reason can be any.

 

h2. Points discussed during call:

# Current Logic: 
## On Exchange disconnection:
### GETS Manager downloads missed messages from disconnected exchange(s) and sends “GREEK_MESSAGE_TRAILER” message to connected clients.
### Client sends “GREEK_HISTORICAL_EXSEGMENT_SEQ_REQ” with values in fields like Sequence number, lLogTime (Precision in seconds) and count of records. Since we use precision in seconds for lLogTime we need to build logic to go back in time and use count of records for matching statistics at both requestor and GETS Manager end. Accordingly GETS Manager responds back with messages using <Head> - <Data> -<Trailer> logic.
## On disconnection/restart/relogin of client/adapter/CC
### Client sends “GREEK_HISTORICAL_EXSEGMENT_SEQ_REQ” with values in fields like Sequence number, lLogTime (Precision in seconds) and count of records. Since we use precision in seconds for lLogTime we have to go back in time and use count of records for matching statistics at both requestor and GETS Manager end. Accordingly GETS Manager responds back with messages using <Head> - <Data> -<Trailer> logic.
# Other points considering current logic:
## Sequence numbers fields 3 digits are reserved for exchange and segment, so only 6 digits are available to store orders sequence numbers, so *we can have maximum 9,99,999 orders.*
## Sequence numbers 3 digits may get changed/corrupted - Eg: 101 changes to 102 which changes segment and may give wrong results.
## Download data will be only for client orders, No Pro orders will be given in download. 
#*Note:* “GNLDealer” is not created as part of user management flow.
# Proposed changes and Impact:
## Proposition: Usage of last activity reference number with nano seconds in GREEK _ORDER_ ENTRY structure to take as reference number for gap fill of missed messages.
## Impact: Considering 2512 release for this changes.
### Shift field for last activity reference number above from its previous position so that it is consumed by Client. Right now this field is not sent to Client.
### Change in compatibility number.
### Ensure Interactive component of all exchanges populates the field last activity reference number with nanoseconds precision from respective field of exchange structure.
### Use of last activity reference number field for gap fill may make lSequenceNo field of GREEK HEADER as redundant. _Can we reuse lSequenceNo field by changing data type to populate value in last activity reference number ?_[^GapFill_DataStructures.docx]

+*Square Off Cancellation:*+

New Message Codes for Square-off Cancellation

* HVTSqOffCancellation = 18
* HVTStopFreshOrder = 19

 

*Process Explanation*:

When the timer is triggered, the system will receive the HVTStopFreshOrder message (code 19).

Upon receipt of the HVTStopFreshOrder message, you must stop accepting fresh orders for the specific ExchangeCode and ProductType provided in the message structure.

When the system receives the HVTSqOffCancellation message (code 18), you must cancel the specific order as indicated by the values provided in the message structure.
